thread_text:
ISSUE #139515: kube-proxy nftables: entire sync fails when any single Service generates a comment exceeding 128 characters
Author: RomanPavelko
Date: 2026-06-05T07:37:46Z
Labels: kind/bug, sig/network, triage/accepted
State: closed

[c0]
__What happened?__

When running kube-proxy in `mode: nftables`, if any Service causes kube-proxy to generate an nftables comment exceeding the Linux kernel's 128-character limit, __the entire nftables transaction is rejected and no service routing rules are applied on that sync cycle__. kube-proxy retries every 30 seconds and fails every time until the offending Service is removed. During this time, __all ClusterIP routing is broken cluster-wide__, including kube-dns.

__How to reproduce__

1. Run a cluster with kube-proxy in `mode: nftables` (recommended default since Kubernetes 1.35)
2. Create a Service where the combined kube-proxy comment string `<namespace>/<service-name>:<port-name>` exceeds 128 characters

A realistic example:

- Namespace: `loft-acme-platform-services-team-dev-v-shared-workloads-ns-001` __(62 chars ✅ valid k8s namespace)__
- Service name: `my-api-svc-x-my-api-namespace-x-acme-shared-vcluster--a1b2c3d4e` __(63 chars ✅ valid k8s service name)__
- kube-proxy comment: `loft-acme-platform-services-team-dev-v-shared-workloads-ns-001/my-api-svc-x-my-api-namespace-x-acme-shared-vcluster--a1b2c3d4e:http` → __131 characters ❌ kernel rejects__

Both the namespace (62 chars) and the service name (63 chars) are individually valid Kubernetes DNS labels (≤63 chars each) and are accepted by the Kubernetes API. It is only the __combined string that kube-proxy constructs for the nftables comment__ — `<namespace>/<name>:<port>` — that exceeds the 128-char kernel limit.

This scenario occurs naturally with tools like __vCluster__, which syncs virtual-cluster Services to the host namespace using the pattern `<svc>-x-<ns>-x-<vcluster>--<hash>`. vCluster correctly truncates the service name to ≤63 chars per Kubernetes spec. However, when combined with a long management namespace name (e.g. `loft-<team>-<env>-v-<vcluster>`), the resulting nftables comment string can exceed 128 characters.

__What you expected to happen__

kube-proxy should either:

- Truncate the nftables comment to ≤128 characters (or omit it entirely) and continue syncing all other service rules successfully, OR
- Skip only the offending Service and continue applying rules for all others

__What actually happened__

kube-proxy logs show the following error on every sync attempt (every 30 seconds):

```javascript
E proxier.go:1788] "nftables sync failed" err=<
    /dev/stdin:1473:84-216: Error: comment too long, 128 characters maximum allowed
    add element ip kube-proxy no-endpoint-services { 10.96.1.100 . tcp . 80 comment "loft-acme-platform-services-team-dev-v-shared-workloads-ns-001/my-api-svc-x-my-api-namespace-x-acme-shared-vcluster--a1b2c3d4e:http" : goto reject-chain }
                                                                                     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
 > ipFamily="IPv4"
I proxier.go:1143] "Sync failed" ipFamily="IPv4" retryingTime="30s"
```

The sync fails __atomically__ — nftables applies rules in a single transaction, so one bad comment causes the __entire ruleset to be rejected__. This means zero ClusterIP routing rules exist on any node during the failure window.

__Impact__

- All Kubernetes Services become unreachable via ClusterIP on all nodes simultaneously
- `kube-dns` ClusterIP is unreachable → DNS stops working for all pods cluster-wide
- Workloads that depend on DNS (e.g. StatefulSets using headless service DNS for peer discovery such as etcd HA clusters) cannot initialize
- The failure is silent from a pod perspective — packets are dropped, not refused with an error
- Only removing the offending Service restores normal operation

__Kubernetes version__

```javascript
Server Version: v1.35.0
```

__kube-proxy mode__

```yaml
mode: nftables
```

__OS / kernel__

Talos Linux, kernel 6.x (nftables native mode)

__Suggested fix__

The nftables comment is purely for human readability — it has no functional effect on routing. The fix should be straightforward: __truncate comment strings to ≤128 characters__ before including them in nftables statements. The iptables proxier does not have this issue.

title: Failure cluster [d7f6dc54...] `Failed to get successful response from /configz: context deadline exceeded`
need_summary: Whether the kubelet crash-loop caused by locking `DisableCPUQuotaWithExclusiveCPUs` is expected or needs a test/update, with the answer anchored on PR #139351 and the cited kubelet config/defaults and e2e test files.
security_topic: regression caused by locked kubelet feature gate crashing startup
question_text: ### Failure cluster [d7f6dc54a335e039ff4b](https://go.k8s.io/triage#d7f6dc54a335e039ff4b) ##### Error text: ``` [FAILED] Failed to get successful response from /configz: context deadline exceeded In [It] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e_node/kubeletconfig/kubeletconfig.go:186 @ 05/30/26 05:26:56.65 ```
answer_text:
## Root cause: #139351 (locking `DisableCPUQuotaWithExclusiveCPUs` to default) — kubelet crash-loop, not a flake

This is a hard regression, not a flake. The `/configz` timeout is a symptom: the kubelet **panics on startup** and crash-loops, so `GetCurrentKubeletConfig` (which polls `https://127.0.0.1:10250/configz` for 5m in the setup of nearly every Serial/resource-manager test) times out with `context deadline exceeded`.

### Regression boundary (first bad build)
Both resource-manager lanes flipped green→red at the same SHAs:

| lane | last green | first red |
|---|---|---|
| `…containerd-resource-managers` | [`a3242d59`](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-containerd-resource-managers/2060478461952135168) (2026-05-29 21:49Z) | [`bb7dec4604f`](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-containerd-resource-managers/2060538860126867456) (2026-05-30 01:49Z) |
| `ci-node-crio-resource-managers` | [`a3242d59`](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-resource-managers/2060486514827071488) (2026-05-29 22:21Z) | [`bb7dec4604f`](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-resource-managers/2060546913320570880) (2026-05-30 02:21Z) |

Commit window `a3242d59..bb7dec4604f` contained 3 PRs; **#139351** is the cause.

### Mechanism
`kubelet.log` from the first red build ends in:

```
panic: failed to merge global and in-flight KubeletConfiguration while setting defaults,
error: cannot set feature gate DisableCPUQuotaWithExclusiveCPUs to false, feature is locked to true

goroutine 1 [running]:
…SetDefaults_KubeletConfiguration  pkg/kubelet/apis/config/v1beta1/defaults.go:72
…DecodeKubeletConfiguration        pkg/kubelet/kubeletconfig/util/codec/codec.go:75
…loadConfigFile                    cmd/kubelet/app/server.go:464
```

1. #139351 added `{Version: "1.37", Default: true, LockToDefault: true}` to `DisableCPUQuotaWithExclusiveCPUs`, so the gate can no longer be set to `false`.
2. `SetDefaults_KubeletConfiguration` (`defaults.go:72`) does `localFeatureGate.SetFromMap(obj.FeatureGates)` and **`panic()`s** on the locked-gate conflict when the kubelet decodes its config file at startup.
3. The CPU Manager e2e test writes the gate unconditionally — `configureCPUManagerInKubelet` (`test/e2e_node/cpu_manager_test.go:4034`) — and the block `When("checking the CFS quota management can be disabled")` sets `disableCPUQuotaWithExclusiveCPUs: false` in its `BeforeEach` (`cpu_manager_test.go:1747`). Restarting the kubelet with that config → panic → crash-loop. The `true` cases are fine (that's the locked default); only the `false` case panics.

Because these are **Serial** suites sharing one kubelet, the wedged node cascades the failure to subsequent CPU/Memory/Topology Manager tests in the same run.

### Confirmed across 4 jobs — runtime/arch/provider independent (rules out infra)
The identical panic appears in:

| job | runtime | arch | provider | first red |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-containerd-resource-managers` | containerd | x86 | GCE | [2060538860126867456](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-containerd-resource-managers/2060538860126867456) |
| `ci-node-crio-resource-managers` | **CRI-O** | x86 | GCE | [2060546913320570880](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-resource-managers/2060546913320570880) |
| `ci-containerd-node-e2e-serial-ec2` | containerd | x86 | **AWS EC2** | [2060518224151187456](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-containerd-node-e2e-serial-ec2/2060518224151187456) |
| `ci-containerd-node-arm64-e2e-serial-ec2` | containerd | **ARM64** | AWS EC2 | [2060536595643109376](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-containerd-node-arm64-e2e-serial-ec2/2060536595643109376) |

### Why presubmit didn't catch it
These node-e2e Serial/resource-manager lanes are periodic post-submit only. #139351's presubmits passed — it updated the unit test (`kuberuntime_container_linux_test.go`) but not the `e2e_node` CPU Manager test that sets the gate to `false`.

### Suggested fix
Same class as #137996 (which did exactly this for `InPlacePodLevelResourcesVerticalScaling`); background in #127477. Either:
- update `test/e2e_node/cpu_manager_test.go` to stop setting `DisableCPUQuotaWithExclusiveCPUs: false` (drop/guard the "CFS quota can be disabled" scenario now that the gate is locked to `true`), or
- revert #139351 until the e2e test is updated.

Separately worth considering: `defaults.go:72` turning a bad gate into a `panic()` crash-loops the kubelet instead of failing with a clean validation error.

Earlier same-signature flake issue (pre-dates this regression): #137995.

/cc @ffromani

## Root cause: #139351 (locking `DisableCPUQuotaWithExclusiveCPUs` to default) — kubelet crash-loop, not a flake

This is a hard regression, not a flake. The `/configz` timeout is a symptom: the kubelet **panics on startup** and crash-loops, so `GetCurrentKubeletConfig` (which polls `https://127.0.0.1:10250/configz` for 5m in the setup of nearly every Serial/resource-manager test) times out with `context deadline exceeded`.

### Regression boundary (first bad build)
Both resource-manager lanes flipped green→red at the same SHAs:

| lane | last green | first red |
|---|---|---|
| `…containerd-resource-managers` | [`a3242d59`](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-containerd-resource-managers/2060478461952135168) (2026-05-29 21:49Z) | [`bb7dec4604f`](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-containerd-resource-managers/2060538860126867456) (2026-05-30 01:49Z) |
| `ci-node-crio-resource-managers` | [`a3242d59`](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-resource-managers/2060486514827071488) (2026-05-29 22:21Z) | [`bb7dec4604f`](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-resource-managers/2060546913320570880) (2026-05-30 02:21Z) |

Commit window `a3242d59..bb7dec4604f` contained 3 PRs; **#139351** is the cause.

### Mechanism
`kubelet.log` from the first red build ends in:

```
panic: failed to merge global and in-flight KubeletConfiguration while setting defaults,
error: cannot set feature gate DisableCPUQuotaWithExclusiveCPUs to false, feature is locked to true

goroutine 1 [running]:
…SetDefaults_KubeletConfiguration  pkg/kubelet/apis/config/v1beta1/defaults.go:72
…DecodeKubeletConfiguration        pkg/kubelet/kubeletconfig/util/codec/codec.go:75
…loadConfigFile                    cmd/kubelet/app/server.go:464
```

1. #139351 added `{Version: "1.37", Default: true, LockToDefault: true}` to `DisableCPUQuotaWithExclusiveCPUs`, so the gate can no longer be set to `false`.
2. `SetDefaults_KubeletConfiguration` (`defaults.go:72`) does `localFeatureGate.SetFromMap(obj.FeatureGates)` and **`panic()`s** on the locked-gate conflict when the kubelet decodes its config file at startup.
3. The CPU Manager e2e test writes the gate unconditionally — `configureCPUManagerInKubelet` (`test/e2e_node/cpu_manager_test.go:4034`) — and the block `When("checking the CFS quota management can be disabled")` sets `disableCPUQuotaWithExclusiveCPUs: false` in its `BeforeEach` (`cpu_manager_test.go:1747`). Restarting the kubelet with that config → panic → crash-loop. The `true` cases are fine (that's the locked default); only the `false` case panics.

Because these are **Serial** suites sharing one kubelet, the wedged node cascades the failure to subsequent CPU/Memory/Topology Manager tests in the same run.

### Confirmed across 4 jobs — runtime/arch/provider independent (rules out infra)
The identical panic appears in:

| job | runtime | arch | provider | first red |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-containerd-resource-managers` | containerd | x86 | GCE | [2060538860126867456](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-containerd-resource-managers/2060538860126867456) |
| `ci-node-crio-resource-managers` | **CRI-O** | x86 | GCE | [2060546913320570880](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-node-crio-resource-managers/2060546913320570880) |
| `ci-containerd-node-e2e-serial-ec2` | containerd | x86 | **AWS EC2** | [2060518224151187456](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-containerd-node-e2e-serial-ec2/2060518224151187456) |
| `ci-containerd-node-arm64-e2e-serial-ec2` | containerd | **ARM64** | AWS EC2 | [2060536595643109376](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-containerd-node-arm64-e2e-serial-ec2/2060536595643109376) |

### Why presubmit didn't catch it
These node-e2e Serial/resource-manager lanes are periodic post-submit only. #139351's presubmits passed — it updated the unit test (`kuberuntime_container_linux_test.go`) but not the `e2e_node` CPU Manager test that sets the gate to `false`.

### Suggested fix
Same class as #137996 (which did exactly this for `InPlacePodLevelResourcesVerticalScaling`); background in #127477. Either:
- update `test/e2e_node/cpu_manager_test.go` to stop setting `DisableCPUQuotaWithExclusiveCPUs: false` (drop/guard the "CFS quota can be disabled" scenario now that the gate is locked to `true`), or
- revert #139351 until the e2e test is updated.

title: Failing job: check-dependency-archived-periodical — github.com/envoyproxy/protoc-gen-validate archived upstream
need_summary: Whether the archived transitive dependency github.com/envoyproxy/protoc-gen-validate should be added to hack/unwanted-dependencies.json, based on the issue’s cited depstat output and the suggested JSON entry.
security_topic: archived dependency transitive impact
question_text:
### Reason for failure (if possible)

`github.com/envoyproxy/protoc-gen-validate` was archived upstream (the project has moved to `protovalidate`). We don't depend on it directly — it enters the module graph transitively via gRPC's xDS support:

- `google.golang.org/grpc` directly requires `github.com/cncf/xds/go` and `github.com/envoyproxy/go-control-plane`, whose generated `*.pb.validate.go` code imports the `protoc-gen-validate/validate` runtime.
- For kubernetes the package is **pruned / never compiled** — `go mod why github.com/envoyproxy/protoc-gen-validate` reports the main module does not need it; it exists only as a `go.mod`/`go.sum`/module-graph entry.
answer_text:
Suggested fix: add it to `spec.unwantedModules` in `hack/unwanted-dependencies.json`, alongside the other archived-but-unavoidable transitive deps (`google/btree`, `flynn/go-shlex`, etc.):

```json
"github.com/envoyproxy/protoc-gen-validate": "unmaintained, archive mode; pulled in transitively by google.golang.org/grpc xDS deps",
```

That flips the periodic job's report for this module from `FAIL:` to `OK:`.

title: ci-kubernetes-unit-golang-tip failing: http2.ConfigureServer no longer registers h2 ALPN under go1.27 (x/net v0.55.0)
need_summary: Whether the Go tip x/net/http2 wrapper path failing to append h2 ALPN is a real bug in production and what upstream fix tracks it, anchored by the filed golang/go issue 79778 and Go net CL 785900.
security_topic: HTTP/2 ALPN registration regression under Go tip
question_text: Under Go tip (identifying as go1.27), `http2.ConfigureServer` therefore no longer registers the h2 ALPN protocol. Tests that use `httptest.Server.StartTLS()` after calling `http2.ConfigureServer` end up with an `http/1.1`-only ALPN list, and the TLS handshake rejects any client that requests h2 with `tls: no application protocol`.
answer_text: filed https://github.com/golang/go/issues/79778 and https://go-review.googlesource.com/c/net/+/785900
thread_text:
ISSUE #139263: ci-kubernetes-unit-golang-tip failing: http2.ConfigureServer no longer registers h2 ALPN under go1.27 (x/net v0.55.0)
Author: dims
Date: 2026-05-24T16:15:41Z
Labels: sig/api-machinery, kind/failing-test, area/code-organization, needs-triage, area/code-organization/future-dependencies, kind/dependency
State: closed

[c0]
Follow-on to #139257. That issue tracked a compile error (`undefined: http2.TrailerPrefix`) introduced under Go tip = go1.27 by the x/net/http2 reshuffle in #139248, and was fixed by bumping to x/net v0.55.0 in #139258. With the build unblocked, a second defect from the same reshuffle is now visible: `ci-kubernetes-unit-golang-tip` is still red, with a different signature.

Multiple apiserver HTTP/2 tests fail with TLS ALPN errors:

```
http: TLS handshake error from 127.0.0.1:...: tls: client requested unsupported application protocols (["h2"])
authentication_test.go:685: Get "https://...": remote error: tls: no application protocol
```

Affected tests include `TestUnauthenticatedHTTP2ClientConnectionClose/*` (all subtests), `TestGracefulTerminationWithKeepListeningDuringGracefulTermination{Disabled,Enabled}`, `TestPreShutdownHooks/*`, `TestMuxAndDiscoveryComplete`, and `TestNew/non-nil_dial_holder+internal`, all in `staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/{server,endpoints/filters}`.

Root cause is in vendored `golang.org/x/net@v0.55.0`. The package now splits its server into two implementations:

- `vendor/golang.org/x/net/http2/server.go` — build tag `!(go1.27 && !http2legacy)`. Its `configureServer` appends `"h2"` and `"http/1.1"` to `s.TLSConfig.NextProtos` at lines 205-209.
- `vendor/golang.org/x/net/http2/server_wrap.go` — build tag `go1.27 && !http2legacy`. Its `configureServer` at lines 26-56 does not touch `NextProtos` at all (and does not nil-init `TLSConfig` either).

Under Go tip (identifying as go1.27), `http2.ConfigureServer` therefore no longer registers the h2 ALPN protocol. Tests that use `httptest.Server.StartTLS()` after calling `http2.ConfigureServer` end up with an `http/1.1`-only ALPN list, and the TLS handshake rejects any client that requests h2 with `tls: no application protocol`. Production apiserver code paths that rely on `http2.ConfigureServer` to wire up ALPN are affected by the same defect, not just tests.

The regression boundary in this job:

- last green: build 2057884102870175744 at `45f714fc36` (2026-05-22T18:00:07Z)
- first red (compile error, fixed by #139258): build 2057944767483875328 at `0f935974ee` (2026-05-22T22:01:10Z)
- first red showing the ALPN failure (immediately after #139258 merged): build 2058186598851284992 at `6790dcf1f6` (2026-05-23T14:02:07Z)
- still red on current HEAD as of build 2058549996172611584 at `e09c6f3997` (2026-05-24T14:06:08Z)

The introducing change is PR #139248. Despite its title ("Bump golang.org/x/crypto to v0.52.0") it also re-vendored `golang.org/x/net/http2/` and brought in the `server_wrap.go`/`transport_wrap.go` go1.27 split that contains the defect.

Possible fixes, in order of preference:

1. Upstream `golang.org/x/net`: add the NextProtos append (and the `if s.TLSConfig == nil` guard) to `server_wrap.go`'s `configureServer` so the go1.27 path matches the legacy path. Then bump to the next x/net release in k8s.
2. Carry a local vendor patch on `vendor/golang.org/x/net/http2/server_wrap.go` (and matching staging modules) until upstream lands.
3. Build with `-tags http2legacy` for the golang-tip job to opt out of the wrapper path; not a fix, but unblocks CI.

Multiple apiserver HTTP/2 tests fail with TLS ALPN errors:

```
http: TLS handshake error from 127.0.0.1:...: tls: client requested unsupported application protocols (["h2"])
authentication_test.go:685: Get "https://...": remote error: tls: no application protocol
```

Affected tests include `TestUnauthenticatedHTTP2ClientConnectionClose/*` (all subtests), `TestGracefulTerminationWithKeepListeningDuringGracefulTermination{Disabled,Enabled}`, `TestPreShutdownHooks/*`, `TestMuxAndDiscoveryComplete`, and `TestNew/non-nil_dial_holder+internal`, all in `staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/{server,endpoints/filters}`.

Root cause is in vendored `golang.org/x/net@v0.55.0`. The package now splits its server into two implementations:

- `vendor/golang.org/x/net/http2/server.go` — build tag `!(go1.27 && !http2legacy)`. Its `configureServer` appends `"h2"` and `"http/1.1"` to `s.TLSConfig.NextProtos` at lines 205-209.
- `vendor/golang.org/x/net/http2/server_wrap.go` — build tag `go1.27 && !http2legacy`. Its `configureServer` at lines 26-56 does not touch `NextProtos` at all (and does not nil-init `TLSConfig` either).

Under Go tip (identifying as go1.27), `http2.ConfigureServer` therefore no longer registers the h2 ALPN protocol. Tests that use `httptest.Server.StartTLS()` after calling `http2.ConfigureServer` end up with an `http/1.1`-only ALPN list, and the TLS handshake rejects any client that requests h2 with `tls: no application protocol`. Production apiserver code paths that rely on `http2.ConfigureServer` to wire up ALPN are affected by the same defect, not just tests.

The regression boundary in this job:

- last green: build 2057884102870175744 at `45f714fc36` (2026-05-22T18:00:07Z)
- first red (compile error, fixed by #139258): build 2057944767483875328 at `0f935974ee` (2026-05-22T22:01:10Z)
- first red showing the ALPN failure (immediately after #139258 merged): build 2058186598851284992 at `6790dcf1f6` (2026-05-23T14:02:07Z)
- still red on current HEAD as of build 2058549996172611584 at `e09c6f3997` (2026-05-24T14:06:08Z)

The introducing change is PR #139248. Despite its title ("Bump golang.org/x/crypto to v0.52.0") it also re-vendored `golang.org/x/net/http2/` and brought in the `server_wrap.go`/`transport_wrap.go` go1.27 split that contains the defect.

Possible fixes, in order of preference:

1. Upstream `golang.org/x/net`: add the NextProtos append (and the `if s.TLSConfig == nil` guard) to `server_wrap.go`'s `configureServer` so the go1.27 path matches the legacy path. Then bump to the next x/net release in k8s.
2. Carry a local vendor patch on `vendor/golang.org/x/net/http2/server_wrap.go` (and matching staging modules) until upstream lands.
3. Build with `-tags http2legacy` for the golang-tip job to opt out of the wrapper path; not a fix, but unblocks CI.

### Scenario

Based on [logs](https://storage.googleapis.com/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kind-dra-n-2/2055003513271881728/artifacts/kind/kind-worker3/kubelet.log):

### Conclusion

So if such scenario - loading newer file format by older kubelet - needs to be supported, then introducing V4 must be redesigned.
Such scenario doesn't work also with lately released kubelet version 1.36 when `PodLevelResourceManagers` is enabled as it saves checkpoint in V3 version, which is not understood by 1.35 and previous. Probably it was not tested with feature gate enabled. With feature gate disabled the checkpoint is saved in V2 format.

[c18] @lukaszwojciechowski 2026-05-15T03:29:41Z:
> See also [#103942 (comment)](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/103942#issuecomment-4364347463) - this is related, isn't it?

yes, that could be one of the ways to do it, but the case is a bit more complex.

The 1.36 release saves checkpoint in:
* V3 - if `PodLevelResourceManagers` feature gate is enabled
* V2 - if `PodLevelResourceManagers` feature gate is disabled
Former releases used V2 and were not aware of `PodLevelResourceManagers` feature gate.

So new checkpoint version format must be designed in a way to cover these cases:

| Case | From | To | PodLevelResourceManagers | Must be in version |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 1.37 | 1.36 | enabled | V3 format _(or is it OK to use V2 format dropping information about PodLevel CPU assignments ? 1.36 even with `PodLevelResourceManagers` enabled will still fallback to V2)_ |
| A | 1.37 | 1.36 | disabled | V2 format |
| A | 1.37 | 1.35 | * | V2 format |

If we can drop information about PodLevelResources, then we can use @pohly your idea by prefixing new format with V2.
As far as I know the documentation says that node needs to be drained during upgrade operations, so there should be no resources allocated anyway.

[EDIT] I checked. It won't work :( because current and older versions of kubelet unmarshal data with `json.Unmarshal` so for `{V2}{V4}` JSON they will return syntax error. To make that work the data need to be parsed by JSON stream

@ffromani What do you think?

I'd expect a downgrade to be supported. This could be relevant in case of unexpected problems that cannot be fixed by flipping feature gates. But maybe special instructions like "drain node first" mitigate this because then the file would be removed? But is it really? In the DRA n-x jobs, the only running pods before the "downgrade" are daemonsets. Would those also get removed by draining the node and is the problematic file then truly gone or merely empty?

> https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/103942#issuecomment-4364347463 ... It won't work :( because current and older versions of kubelet unmarshal data with json.Unmarshal so for {V2}{V4} JSON they will return syntax error.

Darn. Here's a different idea: keep the current format of the file unchanged. Add new fields as necessary **but** calculate the checksum using the traditional struct without the new fields. Assuming that old kubelet doesn't do strict parsing and fails for unknown keys, it should be able to read such a file. The "legacy" checksum won't cover new fields, but quite I don't think that this is a big loss.

[c20] @ffromani 2026-05-15T07:48:34Z:
The problem which I hinted previously and which prompted my revert request was indeed that there's no quick fix missing (#139053) over an overall good platform, but we need to rediscuss and review some key assumptions, and this should happen on a clean slate, not with red CI (red CI should not be normalized).
Therefore I think we should move on with the revert today (May 25) even though the cpumanager state change is still needed and needed ASAP for reasons I'm about to elaborate.

So, the key problem here is actually the cpumanager checkpoint V2 format which is not extensible. Switching the PodLevelResourceManagers FG to true e.g. beta graduation and making the kubelet produce V3 would have caused the exact same issue. This is what I hinted in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/139069#issuecomment-4454472627 - apologies for my terseness, it was late night.

But by all measures the V3 is a worse posture than V4 - less extensible, same or worse problems about forward/backward compatibility. 
Therefore, moving to V4 ASAP is part of the solution, both for the PodLevelResourceManagers graduation and for the upcoming cpumanager work.

@lukaszwojciechowski is correct in the sense that up till now we operated with less strict compatibility constraints: this is what we documented extensively in the KEP which introduced V3, because of the limitation of the **existing** V2 format: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-node/5526-pod-level-resource-managers/README.md#rollout-upgrade-and-rollback-planning (disclosure: I was one of the main reviewers of that KEP).

That said, @pohly raises a very fair point and this issue also keep us honest: if there's merit in all the above conversation about draining for the *static* policy, here the lanes use the *none* policy and the default setting; the out-of-the-box configuration warrants a bit more care, so I'm all for trying harder a better solution building on the foundation of V4.

I can think about two possible enhancements moving forward: they are initial thoughts which must need to validated, and possibly  can be combined to produce a full working solution 
1. build on top of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/139069#issuecomment-4457247538 - V4 computes the checksum of the V2 format and stores in the `Checksum` field, then we add _another_ real checksum like `DataChecksum` for the new Data field - the key point here if `Data` is ignored, so `DataChecksum` should. This way we can be backward compatible, protect both data sets at cost of a bit uglier format. But the checkpoint is kubelet privata data anyway, so it's bearable. When the N-3 kubelet understands V4 format, we can unify the checksums (both will store the same content) or deprecate one of them or somehow simplify again.
2. backport read support for V4, so older kubelets can just read the V4 format. Actually pretty safe: except for the upgrade path, V4 loading is dead code and will never trigger. We can even add a FG to force it off if needed. There's a case for this backport because 1.36, with PodLevelResourceManagers, is arguably already broken in this regard.

All that said, we also need to clarify the kubelet state files compatibility promise. This is a wakeup call about different parties having different, and legit expectations. To be obvious: I'm not saying that backward compat is unachiavable or we should not aim for it. But it's a higher bar we need to prepare to clear and update some processes to achieve.

> Dual-checksum sketch implemented here [#139083](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139083) **for illustration purposes** I'd still go with revert and then replan, revalidate and send a new PR ASAP vs rush a fix with red CI.
>

> [@pohly](https://github.com/pohly) / [@nojnhuh](https://github.com/nojnhuh) green light to merge the revert?

Thank you @ffromani for the sketch. That's exactly the solution I was also thinking about.

### V4 with embedded V2

The drawback of embedding V2 in V4 will be the lost of PodLevel CPU assignments (`PodEntries` field). So reading file created by 1.37 with `PodLevelResourceManagers` enabled by 1.36 with `PodLevelResourceManagers` will lose `PodEntries`.

So with following scenarios we have:
| Version creating checkpoint | Format of checkpoint | Version restoring checkpoint | PodLevelResourceManagers | Result | Issues |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V2 | 1.37 | disabled | valid read of V4 | - |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V2 | 1.37 | enabled | valid read of V4 | - |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V2 | 1.36 | disabled | valid read of V2 | - |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V2 | 1.36 | enabled | fail to verify V3 checksum, fallback to V2,  valid read of V2 | `PodEntries` field is not restored |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V2 | 1.35 | N/A | valid read of V2 | - |

### V4 with embedded V3

We cannot however just use regular V3, because it's checksum won't pass verification in 1.36 with `PodLevelResourceManagers` disabled or e.g. 1.35

But there is one more way we can handle it: Embed V3 but set V3 checksum to 0. With such approach we have:

| Version creating checkpoint | Format of checkpoint | Version restoring checkpoint | PodLevelResourceManagers | Result | Issues |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V3 and checksum=0 | 1.37 | disabled | valid read of V4 | - |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V3 and checksum=0 | 1.37 | enabled | valid read of V4 | - |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V3 and checksum=0 | 1.36 | disabled | valid read of V2 accepting empty checksum| no data consistency verification (empty checksum) |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V3 and checksum=0 | 1.36 | enabled | fail to verify V3 checksum, fallback to V2,  valid read of V2 accepting empty checksum | hackish and no data consistency verification (empty checksum) |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V3 and checksum=0 | 1.35 | N/A | valid read of V2 accepting empty checksum| no data consistency verification (empty checksum) |

#### Why it works

Both 1.36 and 1.35 have special case for empty checksum when verifying V2 checkpoint:
```
func (cp *CPUManagerCheckpointV2) VerifyChecksum() error {
	if cp.Checksum == 0 {
		// accept empty checksum for compatibility with old file backend
		return nil
	}
[...]
```

#### Why it's shady in 1.36 with `PodLevelResourceManagers` enabled
`loadAndMigrateCheckpointV3` in 1.36 works in following steps:

1) tries to load and verify checksum of V3 version first
- it succeeds to load V3 structure
- but fails to verify checksum (the V3 verification does not have special case for empty checksum)
- however the `checkpointV3` variable contain properly read structure including `podEntry`

2) tries to load and verify checksum of V2 version
- it succeeds to load V3 structure as V2 ignoring `podEntry`
- it passes checksum verification (special case for empty checksum)
- `checkpointV2` variable contain all valid V2 fields

3) `migrateV2CheckpointToV3Checkpoint` is called
- which copies all V2 fields from `checkpointV2` to `checkpointV3` 
- so now `checkpointV3` contains all V2 fields read from V2 fromat and PodEntries from V3

It's a bit hackish, but it works. I tested all of the scenarios on my local cluster and for this scenario I got:
```
May 15 11:00:39 kind-kubetest-worker kubelet[798]: I0515 11:00:39.472750     798 state_mem.go:45] "Initialized" logger="CPUManager state checkpoint.CPUManager state memory"
May 15 11:00:39 kind-kubetest-worker kubelet[798]: E0515 11:00:39.472905     798 state_checkpoint.go:203] "V3 checkpoint is corrupt, falling back to V2" err="checkpoint is corrupted" logger="CPUManager state checkpoint"
May 15 11:00:39 kind-kubetest-worker kubelet[798]: I0515 11:00:39.472953     798 state_checkpoint.go:215] "migrating cpu manager checkpoint from v2 to v3" logger="CPUManager state checkpoint"
May 15 11:00:39 kind-kubetest-worker kubelet[798]: I0515 11:00:39.472965     798 state_mem.go:150] "Updated pod CPUSet assignments" logger="CPUManager state checkpoint.CPUManager state memory" assignments={"d0388348-ccc0-4b70-b8fc-137154f2f0ae":{"cpuSet":"1-5"}}
May 15 11:00:39 kind-kubetest-worker kubelet[798]: I0515 11:00:39.472992     798 state_mem.go:123] "Updated default CPUSet" logger="CPUManager state checkpoint.CPUManager state memory" cpuSet="0-7"
May 15 11:00:39 kind-kubetest-worker kubelet[798]: I0515 11:00:39.472999     798 state_mem.go:141] "Updated CPUSet assignments" logger="CPUManager state checkpoint.CPUManager state memory" assignments={}
```

### Decision

So we need to choose between those two designs:
* V4 with embedded V2 - clear solution, but loses PodEntry data
* V4 with embedded V3 - works in all scenarios, but is a bit shady and also does not validate data consistency as checkpoint is zeroed

@ffromani @pohly What is your opinion?

The problem here is this works by coincidence. It's very easy to break and/or create surprising behavior.
I don't think we should sneak in more surprising behavior. Unless the full `PodLevelResourceManagers` backward compat is a must-have (which, it should not be: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/5526-pod-level-resource-managers#rollout-upgrade-and-rollback-planning ) then I'd go with the straightforward v2 embedding.

> See also [#103942 (comment)](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/103942#issuecomment-4364347463) - this is related, isn't it?

yes, that could be one of the ways to do it, but the case is a bit more complex.

The 1.36 release saves checkpoint in:
* V3 - if `PodLevelResourceManagers` feature gate is enabled
* V2 - if `PodLevelResourceManagers` feature gate is disabled
Former releases used V2 and were not aware of `PodLevelResourceManagers` feature gate.

So new checkpoint version format must be designed in a way to cover these cases:

| Case | From | To | PodLevelResourceManagers | Must be in version |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 1.37 | 1.36 | enabled | V3 format _(or is it OK to use V2 format dropping information about PodLevel CPU assignments ? 1.36 even with `PodLevelResourceManagers` enabled will still fallback to V2)_ |
| A | 1.37 | 1.36 | disabled | V2 format |
| A | 1.37 | 1.35 | * | V2 format |

If we can drop information about PodLevelResources, then we can use @pohly your idea by prefixing new format with V2.
As far as I know the documentation says that node needs to be drained during upgrade operations, so there should be no resources allocated anyway.

[EDIT] I checked. It won't work :( because current and older versions of kubelet unmarshal data with `json.Unmarshal` so for `{V2}{V4}` JSON they will return syntax error. To make that work the data need to be parsed by JSON stream

@ffromani What do you think?

comments.author: ffromani
comments.body:
The problem which I hinted previously and which prompted my revert request was indeed that there's no quick fix missing (#139053) over an overall good platform, but we need to rediscuss and review some key assumptions, and this should happen on a clean slate, not with red CI (red CI should not be normalized).
Therefore I think we should move on with the revert today (May 25) even though the cpumanager state change is still needed and needed ASAP for reasons I'm about to elaborate.

So, the key problem here is actually the cpumanager checkpoint V2 format which is not extensible. Switching the PodLevelResourceManagers FG to true e.g. beta graduation and making the kubelet produce V3 would have caused the exact same issue. This is what I hinted in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/139069#issuecomment-4454472627 - apologies for my terseness, it was late night.

But by all measures the V3 is a worse posture than V4 - less extensible, same or worse problems about forward/backward compatibility. 
Therefore, moving to V4 ASAP is part of the solution, both for the PodLevelResourceManagers graduation and for the upcoming cpumanager work.

@lukaszwojciechowski is correct in the sense that up till now we operated with less strict compatibility constraints: this is what we documented extensively in the KEP which introduced V3, because of the limitation of the **existing** V2 format: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-node/5526-pod-level-resource-managers/README.md#rollout-upgrade-and-rollback-planning (disclosure: I was one of the main reviewers of that KEP).

That said, @pohly raises a very fair point and this issue also keep us honest: if there's merit in all the above conversation about draining for the *static* policy, here the lanes use the *none* policy and the default setting; the out-of-the-box configuration warrants a bit more care, so I'm all for trying harder a better solution building on the foundation of V4.

I can think about two possible enhancements moving forward: they are initial thoughts which must need to validated, and possibly  can be combined to produce a full working solution 
1. build on top of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/139069#issuecomment-4457247538 - V4 computes the checksum of the V2 format and stores in the `Checksum` field, then we add _another_ real checksum like `DataChecksum` for the new Data field - the key point here if `Data` is ignored, so `DataChecksum` should. This way we can be backward compatible, protect both data sets at cost of a bit uglier format. But the checkpoint is kubelet privata data anyway, so it's bearable. When the N-3 kubelet understands V4 format, we can unify the checksums (both will store the same content) or deprecate one of them or somehow simplify again.
2. backport read support for V4, so older kubelets can just read the V4 format. Actually pretty safe: except for the upgrade path, V4 loading is dead code and will never trigger. We can even add a FG to force it off if needed. There's a case for this backport because 1.36, with PodLevelResourceManagers, is arguably already broken in this regard.

All that said, we also need to clarify the kubelet state files compatibility promise. This is a wakeup call about different parties having different, and legit expectations. To be obvious: I'm not saying that backward compat is unachiavable or we should not aim for it. But it's a higher bar we need to prepare to clear and update some processes to achieve.

comments.author: lukaszwojciechowski
comments.body:
> Dual-checksum sketch implemented here [#139083](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139083) **for illustration purposes** I'd still go with revert and then replan, revalidate and send a new PR ASAP vs rush a fix with red CI.
> 
> I'm biased, but the sketch turned out less ugly than I anticipated. May be viable after all, granted it actually works. Still to be verified. Thoughts?
> 
> [@pohly](https://github.com/pohly) / [@nojnhuh](https://github.com/nojnhuh) green light to merge the revert?

Thank you @ffromani for the sketch. That's exactly the solution I was also thinking about.

### V4 with embedded V2

The drawback of embedding V2 in V4 will be the lost of PodLevel CPU assignments (`PodEntries` field). So reading file created by 1.37 with `PodLevelResourceManagers` enabled by 1.36 with `PodLevelResourceManagers` will lose `PodEntries`.

So with following scenarios we have:
| Version creating checkpoint | Format of checkpoint | Version restoring checkpoint | PodLevelResourceManagers | Result | Issues |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V2 | 1.37 | disabled | valid read of V4 | - |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V2 | 1.37 | enabled | valid read of V4 | - |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V2 | 1.36 | disabled | valid read of V2 | - |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V2 | 1.36 | enabled | fail to verify V3 checksum, fallback to V2,  valid read of V2 | `PodEntries` field is not restored |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V2 | 1.35 | N/A | valid read of V2 | - |

### V4 with embedded V3

We cannot however just use regular V3, because it's checksum won't pass verification in 1.36 with `PodLevelResourceManagers` disabled or e.g. 1.35

But there is one more way we can handle it: Embed V3 but set V3 checksum to 0. With such approach we have:

| Version creating checkpoint | Format of checkpoint | Version restoring checkpoint | PodLevelResourceManagers | Result | Issues |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V3 and checksum=0 | 1.37 | disabled | valid read of V4 | - |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V3 and checksum=0 | 1.37 | enabled | valid read of V4 | - |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V3 and checksum=0 | 1.36 | disabled | valid read of V2 accepting empty checksum| no data consistency verification (empty checksum) |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V3 and checksum=0 | 1.36 | enabled | fail to verify V3 checksum, fallback to V2,  valid read of V2 accepting empty checksum | hackish and no data consistency verification (empty checksum) |
| 1.37 | V4 with embedded V3 and checksum=0 | 1.35 | N/A | valid read of V2 accepting empty checksum| no data consistency verification (empty checksum) |

#### Why it works

Both 1.36 and 1.35 have special case for empty checksum when verifying V2 checkpoint:
```
func (cp *CPUManagerCheckpointV2) VerifyChecksum() error {
	if cp.Checksum == 0 {
		// accept empty checksum for compatibility with old file backend
		return nil
	}
[...]
```

#### Why it's shady in 1.36 with `PodLevelResourceManagers` enabled
`loadAndMigrateCheckpointV3` in 1.36 works in following steps:

1) tries to load and verify checksum of V3 version first
- it succeeds to load V3 structure
- but fails to verify checksum (the V3 verification does not have special case for empty checksum)
- however the `checkpointV3` variable contain properly read structure including `podEntry`

2) tries to load and verify checksum of V2 version
- it succeeds to load V3 structure as V2 ignoring `podEntry`
- it passes checksum verification (special case for empty checksum)
- `checkpointV2` variable contain all valid V2 fields

3) `migrateV2CheckpointToV3Checkpoint` is called
- which copies all V2 fields from `checkpointV2` to `checkpointV3` 
- so now `checkpointV3` contains all V2 fields read from V2 fromat and PodEntries from V3

It's a bit hackish, but it works. I tested all of the scenarios on my local cluster and for this scenario I got:
```
May 15 11:00:39 kind-kubetest-worker kubelet[798]: I0515 11:00:39.472750     798 state_mem.go:45] "Initialized" logger="CPUManager state checkpoint.CPUManager state memory"
May 15 11:00:39 kind-kubetest-worker kubelet[798]: E0515 11:00:39.472905     798 state_checkpoint.go:203] "V3 checkpoint is corrupt, falling back to V2" err="checkpoint is corrupted" logger="CPUManager state checkpoint"
May 15 11:00:39 kind-kubetest-worker kubelet[798]: I0515 11:00:39.472953     798 state_checkpoint.go:215] "migrating cpu manager checkpoint from v2 to v3" logger="CPUManager state checkpoint"
May 15 11:00:39 kind-kubetest-worker kubelet[798]: I0515 11:00:39.472965     798 state_mem.go:150] "Updated pod CPUSet assignments" logger="CPUManager state checkpoint.CPUManager state memory" assignments={"d0388348-ccc0-4b70-b8fc-137154f2f0ae":{"cpuSet":"1-5"}}
May 15 11:00:39 kind-kubetest-worker kubelet[798]: I0515 11:00:39.472992     798 state_mem.go:123] "Updated default CPUSet" logger="CPUManager state checkpoint.CPUManager state memory" cpuSet="0-7"
May 15 11:00:39 kind-kubetest-worker kubelet[798]: I0515 11:00:39.472999     798 state_mem.go:141] "Updated CPUSet assignments" logger="CPUManager state checkpoint.CPUManager state memory" assignments={}
```

### Decision

So we need to choose between those two designs:
* V4 with embedded V2 - clear solution, but loses PodEntry data
* V4 with embedded V3 - works in all scenarios, but is a bit shady and also does not validate data consistency as checkpoint is zeroed

@ffromani @pohly What is your opinion?

The problem here is this works by coincidence. It's very easy to break and/or create surprising behavior.
I don't think we should sneak in more surprising behavior. Unless the full `PodLevelResourceManagers` backward compat is a must-have (which, it should not be: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/5526-pod-level-resource-managers#rollout-upgrade-and-rollback-planning ) then I'd go with the straightforward v2 embedding.

title: After switching the Go version to 1.26.1, the binary package has become significantly larger.
need_summary: Whether the binary size regression under Go 1.26.1 is caused by the protobuf-go issue fixed in PR #137451 (commit c8826e0d235) and tracked in k8s #137445.
security_topic: build-size regression with Go version compatibility and grpcnotrace behavior
question_text: The effect of -tags "grpcnotrace" should be the same in Go 1.26.1 and Go 1.24.6, and the binary size should not change significantly.
answer_text: release-1.34 does not claim support for go 1.26 yet, official releases use the .go-version to build.
thread_text:
ISSUE #138962: After switching the Go version to 1.26.1, the binary package has become significantly larger.
Author: molinsoma
Date: 2026-05-11T11:55:47Z
Labels: kind/bug, sig/architecture, needs-triage
State: closed

[c0]
### What happened?

The Kubernetes 1.34.1 code is used to compile a binary file using Go 1.24.6. The compilation command is as follows:
go build -ldflags "-s -w" -tags "grpcnotrace" -o _output/bin/kube-apiserver cmd/kube-apiserver/apiserver.go
Then, the binary file is compiled using Go 1.26.1. It is found that the size of the kube-apiserver binary file compiled using Go 1.24.6 is 85233956,
while the size of the kube-apiserver binary file compiled using Go 1.26.1 is 103235849, which is 18 MB larger than that of the binary file compiled using Go 1.24.6. This is unreasonable.
In addition, after I removed -tags "grpcnotrace", the size of the binary file compiled using Go 1.24.6 was 102572324, and the size of the binary file compiled using Go 1.26.1 was 103534857. That is, the -tags "grpcnotrace" option was very effective in Go 1.24.6, but had almost no effect in Go 1.26.1.

### What did you expect to happen?

The effect of -tags "grpcnotrace" should be the same in Go 1.26.1 and Go 1.24.6, and the binary size should not change significantly.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run the go build -ldflags "-s -w" -tags "grpcnotrace" -o _output/bin/kube-apiserver cmd/kube-apiserver/apiserver.go command to compile the binary file in go1.24.6 and go1.26.1, and then compare the sizes of the two binary files.

title: ImageLocality counts ImageVolume images in raw score but not in max threshold
need_summary: Whether ImageLocality scoring incorrectly counted ImageVolume images in the raw score but not in the max threshold, and the answer rests on the linked fixing PR #138951 and the cited calculatePriority/ImageVolume code path.
security_topic: ImageLocality scoring inconsistency for ImageVolume images
question_text:
PR #130231 updated the `ImageLocality` plugin to account for ImageVolume images when scoring nodes.

However, the current implementation appears to include ImageVolume images only in the raw image score calculation, but not in the image count used to derive the max score threshold.

In `Score`, `imageScores` is calculated by `sumImageScores(nodeInfo, pod, totalNumNodes)`:

```go
imageScores := sumImageScores(nodeInfo, pod, totalNumNodes)

score := calculatePriority(imageScores, len(pod.Spec.InitContainers)+len(pod.Spec.Containers))
```

After #130231, sumImageScores includes image volumes:

```go
for _, volume := range pod.Spec.Volumes {
	if volume.Image == nil {
		continue
	}

	if state, ok := nodeInfo.GetImageStates()[normalizedImageName(volume.Image.Reference)]; ok {
		sum += scaledImageScore(state, totalNumNodes)
	}
}
```

But the second argument passed to calculatePriority still counts only init containers and regular containers:

```go
len(pod.Spec.InitContainers) + len(pod.Spec.Containers)
```
calculatePriority then uses this count to derive the max threshold:

```go
maxThreshold := maxContainerThreshold * int64(numContainers)
```

This means ImageVolume images increase the raw image score, but do not increase the max threshold. As a result, Pods using ImageVolume can receive a higher ImageLocality score, or reach MaxNodeScore more easily, because ImageVolume images are counted in the numerator but not in the threshold.

@sujoshua: Closing this issue.

thread_text:
ISSUE #138952: ImageLocality counts ImageVolume images in raw score but not in max threshold
Author: sujoshua
Date: 2026-05-11T04:57:35Z
Labels: kind/bug, sig/scheduling, triage/accepted
State: closed

[c0]
### What happened?

PR #130231 updated the `ImageLocality` plugin to account for ImageVolume images when scoring nodes.

However, the current implementation appears to include ImageVolume images only in the raw image score calculation, but not in the image count used to derive the max score threshold.

In `Score`, `imageScores` is calculated by `sumImageScores`:

```go
imageScores := sumImageScores(nodeInfo, pod, totalNumNodes)

score := calculatePriority(imageScores, len(pod.Spec.InitContainers)+len(pod.Spec.Containers))
```

After #130231, sumImageScores includes image volumes:

```go
for _, volume := range pod.Spec.Volumes {
	if volume.Image == nil {
		continue
	}

	if state, ok := nodeInfo.GetImageStates()[normalizedImageName(volume.Image.Reference)]; ok {
		sum += scaledImageScore(state, totalNumNodes)
	}
}
```

But the second argument passed to calculatePriority still counts only init containers and regular containers:

```go
len(pod.Spec.InitContainers) + len(pod.Spec.Containers)
```
calculatePriority then uses this count to derive the max threshold:

```go
maxThreshold := maxContainerThreshold * int64(numContainers)
```

This means ImageVolume images increase the raw image score, but do not increase the max threshold. As a result, Pods using ImageVolume can receive a higher ImageLocality score, or reach MaxNodeScore more easily, because ImageVolume images are counted in the numerator but not in the threshold.

### What did you expect to happen?

I think this is a bug because, from the perspective of ImageLocality scoring, a container image and an ImageVolume image have the same locality effect: both are images required by the Pod, and both can avoid image pulling cost if they already exist on the node.

Therefore, ImageVolume images should be counted consistently in ImageLocality scoring.

Since #130231 made ImageVolume images contribute to sumImageScores, they should also contribute to the image count passed to calculatePriority.

The image count should be based on:

```go
len(pod.Spec.InitContainers) + len(pod.Spec.Containers) + numberOfImageVolumes
```

rather than only:

```go
len(pod.Spec.InitContainers) + len(pod.Spec.Containers)
```

With this behavior, a Pod with one regular container image plus one ImageVolume image would be scored consistently with a Pod that has the same two images as regular container images.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Use a Pod with one regular container image and one ImageVolume image.

For example:

```go
testImageVolume := v1.PodSpec{
	Containers: []v1.Container{
		{
			Image: "gcr.io/30",
		},
	},
	Volumes: []v1.Volume{
		{
			Name: "imageVolume",
			VolumeSource: v1.VolumeSource{
				Image: &v1.ImageVolumeSource{
					Reference: "gcr.io/300",
				},
			},
		},
	},
}
```

Assume there are two nodes:

```go
nodes := []*v1.Node{
	makeImageNode("node1", node300600900),
	makeImageNode("node2", node400030),
}
```

For node1, the ImageVolume image gcr.io/300:latest is already present.

Current behavior calculates the score as if there were only one image source:

```
100 * (300M * 1/2 - 23M) / (1000M - 23M) = 12
```

If ImageVolume images are included in the image count, the score should be calculated with two image sources:

```
100 * (300M * 1/2 - 23M) / (1000M * 2 - 23M) = 6
```

This would make the ImageVolume case consistent with a Pod that has the same two images as regular container images.

pr #138951 to fix

Therefore, ImageVolume images should be counted consistently in ImageLocality scoring.

Since #130231 made ImageVolume images contribute to sumImageScores, they should also contribute to the image count passed to calculatePriority.

The image count should be based on:

```go
len(pod.Spec.InitContainers) + len(pod.Spec.Containers) + numberOfImageVolumes
```

rather than only:

```go
len(pod.Spec.InitContainers) + len(pod.Spec.Containers)
```

With this behavior, a Pod with one regular container image plus one ImageVolume image would be scored consistently with a Pod that has the same two images as regular container images.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Use a Pod with one regular container image and one ImageVolume image.

For example:

```go
testImageVolume := v1.PodSpec{
	Containers: []v1.Container{
		{
			Image: "gcr.io/30",
		},
	},
	Volumes: []v1.Volume{
		{
			Name: "imageVolume",
			VolumeSource: v1.VolumeSource{
				Image: &v1.ImageVolumeSource{
					Reference: "gcr.io/300",
				},
			},
		},
	},
}
```

Assume there are two nodes:

```go
nodes := []*v1.Node{
	makeImageNode("node1", node300600900),
	makeImageNode("node2", node400030),
}
```

For node1, the ImageVolume image gcr.io/300:latest is already present.

Current behavior calculates the score as if there were only one image source:

```
100 * (300M * 1/2 - 23M) / (1000M - 23M) = 12
```

If ImageVolume images are included in the image count, the score should be calculated with two image sources:

```
100 * (300M * 1/2 - 23M) / (1000M * 2 - 23M) = 6
```

This would make the ImageVolume case consistent with a Pod that has the same two images as regular container images.

### Anything else we need to know?

title: C++ Naming Collision with `Signal` Enum in CRI API
need_summary: Whether the CRI API enum names need to be renamed to avoid C++ preprocessor macro collisions, anchored by the protobuf style guide on enum value prefixing and the `api.proto` issue discussion.
security_topic: proto enum naming collision with C++ macros
question_text: Looking for opinions from @haircommander @samuelkarp @mikebrow @saschagrunert as the rename is a breaking change.
answer_text:
https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/style/#enum-value-prefixing

Most Kubernetes .proto are generated from the Go code and can't be used without special tooling anyhow (the rest APIs), but for gRPC / CRI I think we should generally defer to the style guide (which suggests the prefixing approach for enum values).

> My understanding of the proto wire protocol is that it only uses these names in code, not on the wire. So names will be different, but everything will work with both namings (as long as we are not changing number and order of enum values)

+1.
thread_text:
ISSUE #138826: C++ Naming Collision with `Signal` Enum in CRI API
Author: SergeyKanzhelev
Date: 2026-05-06T18:39:07Z
Labels: kind/bug, sig/node, needs-triage
State: closed

[c0]
/sig node
/kind bug

TL;DR; Signal enum in CRI API proto generates names the conflict with C++ macros. The best way to fix it is to rename those to `SIGNAL_SIGABRT` instead of just `SIGABRT`. Renaming them is a breaking change, but will simplify life of downstream. Looking for opinions from @haircommander @samuelkarp @mikebrow @saschagrunert  as the rename is a breaking change.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/43fe7b425091a6581e0f6777ef89a215e229eebb/staging/src/k8s.io/cri-api/pkg/apis/runtime/v1/api.proto#L1298-L1301


*AI helped to prepare this following report*

The `Signal` enum introduced in `pkg/apis/runtime/v1/api.proto` contains values that directly match POSIX signal names (e.g., `SIGABRT`, `SIGKILL`, `SIGTERM`, etc.).

When generating C++ code from this Protobuf definition (e.g., using `protoc-gen-cpp`), the resulting C++ header files contain these names as enum constants.

In C++, these names are typically `#define`d macros in standard system headers (like `<signal.h>` or `<csignal>`), which are often transitively included in many projects.

When the generated Protobuf header is included in a C++ project, the preprocessor replaces the enum names with their macro values (e.g., `SIGABRT` becomes `6`), leading to compilation errors. This happens because C++ preprocessor macros do not respect C++ namespaces or scopes.

## How to Reproduce

### 1. Generate C++ files using `protoc`

Given `api.proto` containing:

```proto
syntax = "proto3";

package runtime.v1;

enum Signal {
  RUNTIME_DEFAULT = 0;
  SIGABRT = 1;
  SIGALRM = 2;
  // ... other signals
}

message StopContainerRequest {
  string container_id = 1;
  int64 timeout = 2;
  Signal stop_signal = 3;
}
```

Generate the C++ bindings using `protoc`:

```bash
protoc --cpp_out=. api.proto
```

This produces `api.pb.h` and `api.pb.cc` (or `api.proto.h` depending on the protoc version).

### 2. Example C++ Program

Create a small C++ program `main.cc` that includes the generated header along with standard system headers:

```cpp
#include <csignal> // Includes <signal.h> which defines SIGABRT, etc.
#include <iostream>
#include "api.pb.h" // Or api.proto.h

int main() {
    // Attempt to use the enum
    runtime::v1::Signal s = runtime::v1::Signal::SIGABRT;
    std::cout << "Signal: " << s << std::endl;
    return 0;
}
```

### 3. Compile and Observe the Error

Compile with `g++`:

```bash
g++ -std=c++17 -I. main.cc api.pb.cc -lprotobuf
```

You will see compilation errors similar to:

```
api.pb.h:3695:3: error: expected identifier
 3695 |   SIGABRT = 1,
      |   ^
signal-generic.h:50:18: note: expanded from macro 'SIGABRT'
   50 | #define SIGABRT         6       /* Abnormal termination.  */
```

And in `main.cc`:

```
main.cc:7:50: error: expected unqualified-id
    runtime::v1::Signal s = runtime::v1::Signal::SIGABRT;
                                                 ^
```

## Why This Happens

The C++ preprocessor runs before the compiler parses the code. When it sees `#define SIGABRT 6` in `<signal.h>`, it steps in and blindly replaces all subsequent occurrences of the `SIGABRT` token with `6` globally - bypassing any Protobuf package namespaces or Class scopes.

When parsing the generated Protobuf header:
```cpp
enum Signal {
    SIGABRT = 1,
};
```
Becomes:
```cpp
enum Signal {
    6 = 1, // Syntax error
};
```

And usages:
```cpp
runtime::v1::Signal::SIGABRT
```
Become:
```cpp
runtime::v1::Signal::6
```

## Impact

This prevents `api.proto` from being readily consumed by C++ projects or projects with C++ interop layers without applying fragile `#undef` patches or rewriting headers.

## Proposed Solution / Recommendation

To avoid collisions with preprocessor macros in C and C++, enum values should avoid using common macro names verbatim. This aligns with general Protobuf Style and Best Practices regarding C++ macro constants.

A common practice is to prefix the enum values with the enum type name or another clarifying prefix.

For example, renaming:

```proto
enum Signal {
  RUNTIME_DEFAULT = 0;
  SIGABRT = 1;
  SIGALRM = 2;
  // ...
}
```

To:

```proto
enum Signal {
  RUNTIME_DEFAULT = 0;
  SIGNAL_SIGABRT = 1;
  SIGNAL_SIGALRM = 2;
  // ...
}
```

Or dropping the `SIG` prefix if it's redundant with the enum name:

```proto
enum Signal {
  RUNTIME_DEFAULT = 0;
  SIGNAL_ABRT = 1;
  SIGNAL_ALRM = 2;
  // ...
}
```

This ensures that the generated C++ code does not collide with standard macros.

## Workarounds

In the short term, downstream C++ consumers must `#undef` these macros before including the generated headers (or use `#pragma push_macro`), which is fragile. Renaming them is the cleanest solution.

title: kubelet serving-certificate rotation silently skipped on a subset of v1.34 nodes — no CSR, no errors, no logs
need_summary: Whether the kubelet serving-certificate expiration alert on EKS is expected behavior due to the 45-day signer lifetime and rotation jitter, with the answer anchored on the AWS EKS certificate-signing docs and the kubelet certificate manager jitter range.
security_topic: whether kubelet serving-certificate rotation is actually broken or just delayed by rotation jitter relative to EKS certificate lifetime
question_text: On EKS clusters running kubelet `v1.34.4-eks-f69f56f` on Bottlerocket 1.57.0 (`aws-k8s-1.34`), a subset of nodes appear to silently skip serving-certificate rotation entirely.
answer_text:
The actual situation on the affected node:

- Cert `NotAfter` ≈ `now + 6.97d`, lifetime = 45d → `NotBefore ≈ now − 38.03d`.
- `nextRotationDeadline` returns `NotBefore + jitteryDuration(45d)`, where `jitteryDuration ∈ [0.7, 0.9) × 45d = [31.5d, 40.5d)`.
- The timer hasn't fired, so the jitter value must be ≥ 38.03/45 = **0.845**. Deadline is somewhere in the next ≤ 2.47 days, still comfortably before expiry.
- Rotation will happen on its own before the cert actually expires.

The alert I was chasing (`KubeletServerCertificateExpiration`, threshold < 7d) fires naturally when jitter lands in `[0.844, 0.9)` of the cert lifetime, because:

- EKS hard-caps `kubernetes.io/kubelet-serving` certs at **45 days** (per [AWS EKS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/cert-signing.html)).
- Kubelet's rotation jitter ends at `0.9 × lifetime = 40.5d`, i.e. a rotation wake-up as late as **4.5 days before expiry**.
- The Prometheus-operator alert threshold is **7 days**.
thread_text:
ISSUE #138763: kubelet serving-certificate rotation silently skipped on a subset of v1.34 nodes — no CSR, no errors, no logs
Author: mlushpenko
Date: 2026-05-04T18:13:11Z
Labels: needs-sig, needs-triage
State: closed

[c0]
### What happened?

On EKS clusters running kubelet `v1.34.4-eks-f69f56f` on Bottlerocket 1.57.0 (`aws-k8s-1.34`), a subset of nodes appear to silently skip serving-certificate rotation entirely.

The initial bootstrap CSR is issued at node boot and approved normally by EKS's built-in CSR approver. After that, for the full life of the affected node (38+ days observed):

- `kubelet_certificate_manager_server_rotation_seconds_count` stays at `0`.
- `kubelet_server_expiration_renew_errors == 0`.
- No CSR is ever submitted from the node (`kubectl get csr` shows none from the affected node while sibling nodes' CSRs exist and are approved).
- `journalctl -u kubelet --since -40d | grep -iE "certificate_manager|csr|rotat|serving cert"` returns only the initial-bootstrap `"no serving certificate available for the kubelet"` TLS handshake errors from the first minute of boot. Nothing afterward.
- The serving cert's `NotAfter` passes through the usual rotation threshold (~day 30 of its ~45-day lifetime) without any attempt, and eventually triggers the `KubeletServerCertificateExpiration` alert.

Only one cert file exists on disk:

```
-rw-------.  1 root root 1256 Mar 27 15:34 kubelet-server-2026-03-27-15-34-40.pem
lrwxrwxrwx.  1 root root   59 Mar 27 15:34 kubelet-server-current.pem -> .../kubelet-server-2026-03-27-15-34-40.pem
```

Kubelet PID is unchanged for the full 38 days (process never restarted/crashed). Node is `Ready`, heartbeats OK, `node.status.addresses` populated on the API server.

I'm not 100% sure this is a kubelet bug rather than something I've missed in our setup — posting cautiously in case someone more familiar with the cert-manager code can sanity-check. I believe I've ruled out the usual config/infra suspects (see "Anything else" below).

**Related, already-closed issues/PRs I reviewed:**

- #130001 (Kubelet serving CSR never created)
- #130415 (node reports Ready before server CSR created → templates never populate)
- #130409 (link-local IPv6 → no addresses → no CSR)
- Fix PR #130362 "Use node addresses from informer in kubelet certificate manager" (merged 2025-04-25, confirmed present in v1.34.4 via `git log --contains`)

The symptom here is in the same family as #130415 but on the *rotation* path rather than initial bootstrap (the initial bootstrap CSR *does* succeed). So I suspect the 2025-04 fix may not fully cover the rotation-deadline path.

**Speculative root-cause trace (please sanity-check):**

Tracing v1.34.4:

- `pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go:900` constructs the server cert manager with `klet.getLastObservedNodeAddresses` as the `getAddresses` callback.
- `pkg/kubelet/kubelet_getters.go:472` implements it as `kl.GetNode()` → `kl.nodeLister.Get(nodeName)` on a per-node field-selector-filtered SharedInformer (`pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go:465-475`).
- `pkg/kubelet/certificate/kubelet.go:47` `newGetTemplateFn` returns `nil` when `len(ips) == 0`.
- `staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/util/certificate/certificate_manager.go:449-452`:

  ```go
  // Don't enter rotateCerts and trigger backoff if we don't even have a template to request yet
  if m.getTemplate() == nil {
      return
  }
  ```

If at the moment the rotation deadline fires the per-node informer transiently returns an empty `status.addresses` (or the goroutine evaluating `getTemplate()` races with informer re-list/resync), the rotation function `return`s **without rescheduling**. The only way it re-enters is via a template-changed watch event — so if no subsequent event makes the template transition (informer already settled at the same state), the rotation loop never re-fires for the lifetime of the kubelet.

That code shape — a silent early return with no retry timer — would explain the exact pattern we see (zero attempts, zero errors, zero logs, across 38 days of uptime). PR #130362 moved the *initial* template sourcing off a field that depended on the node-status-update loop, but the rotation-deadline path still depends on `nodeLister.Get()` returning a populated `status.addresses`.

I may be wrong about the root cause — if someone who knows this code can confirm/deny the race, I'd be happy to add `klog.V(2)` around the `return` at `:449` to distinguish "template nil" from "template matches last" on long-running nodes.

### What did you expect to happen?

Either:

- The cert-manager wakes at `nextRotationDeadline` (~day 30 of a 45-day cert), submits a CSR, and logs `"Certificate rotation deadline determined"` / `"Certificate template changed, rotating"` from `staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/util/certificate/certificate_manager.go`;

- OR a failure increments `kubelet_server_expiration_renew_errors` with a descriptive log line.

On the affected nodes, neither happens — the rotation loop appears to either never start or to exit early before reaching `rotateCerts`, and stays silent for the rest of the node's life.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I don't have a deterministic reproducer — it looks probabilistic at boot.

Environment where it reliably reproduces at roughly 15–20% per-node rate:

1. EKS 1.34 control plane (tested with `v1.34.6-eks-bbe087e`).
2. Bottlerocket `aws-k8s-1.34` v1.57.0 nodes, kubelet `v1.34.4-eks-f69f56f`.
3. Kubelet config: `serverTLSBootstrap: true`, default `RotateKubeletServerCertificate` (enabled), no flag overrides.
4. EKS built-in kube-controller-manager CSR auto-approver (no external approver needed — sibling nodes' CSRs approve with message `"Auto approving self kubelet server certificate after SubjectAccessReview"` which matches upstream `pkg/controller/certificates/approver/sarapprove.go`).
5. Karpenter-managed on-demand nodes.

Observation procedure on any long-lived node:

```
# On apiserver
kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/<node>/proxy/metrics" \
  | grep -E 'kubelet_certificate_manager_server_(ttl_seconds|rotation_seconds_count)|kubelet_server_expiration_renew_errors'

# On node (via Bottlerocket admin container):
sheltie ls -la /var/lib/kubelet/pki/
sheltie journalctl -u kubelet --since $(boot-time) | grep -iE "certificate_manager|csr|rotat|serving cert"
```

Across a prod cluster of ~115 non-Fargate nodes, 6 system-nodes booted within the same minute from the same AMI / same NodePool / same IAM role / same kubelet config:

- 5 rotated cleanly at ~day 35 (`rotation_seconds_count == 1`, matching CSR present and approved).
- 1 did not (`rotation_seconds_count == 0` at day 38, no CSR ever requested).

Fleet-wide across four EKS 1.34 clusters: ~15–20% of nodes that survive past the rotation window silently fail to rotate. Most of our churn replaces nodes before the rotation window fires, which is why the bug is easy to miss on faster-churning clusters.

Happy to capture additional diagnostics on a confirmed-affected node if it would help — goroutine dump, `klog -v=4` after kubelet restart (though restart may mask the bug), captured CSR history from siblings, etc.

### Anything else we need to know?

**Config I was able to rule out before posting:**

- `serverTLSBootstrap: true` in kubelet config (Bottlerocket ships this default in `sources/shared-defaults/kubernetes-aws.toml`), confirmed via `apiclient get settings.kubernetes.server-tls-bootstrap`.
- `RotateKubeletServerCertificate` feature gate — GA since 1.12, enabled by default, no flag overrides on our end.
- `rotateCertificates` — default `true` in `KubeletConfiguration`.
- EKS CSR auto-approver is working (same cluster, same approver, approves 5/6 sibling CSRs cleanly).
- RBAC / IAM — identical to siblings that rotate fine.
- Node clock — node posts heartbeats correctly.

Six sibling nodes booted **within the same minute** from the same Karpenter NodeClass (identical AMI, kubelet flags, NodePool, IAM role, subnet, VPC). Five rotated; one didn't. That isolates the fault to kubelet-internal rotation logic, not our config / approver / infra.

**Fleet-wide impact** (for sense of scope, not for dramatic effect):

- Prod `application` cluster: 101/115 non-Fargate nodes currently have `rotation_seconds_count=0`. Most are too young to have entered the rotation window — the bug is latent, only materializing on nodes that survive past ~day 30–35.
- Our workaround: reducing Karpenter `expireAfter` from 100d to 35d to guarantee nodes are replaced before the rotation window is ever reached. This avoids the alert but doesn't surface the underlying bug.

**Why I chose "probably a bug" rather than user error:** given identical config across 6 nodes with 5 rotating cleanly, I don't see a config-level explanation. Happy to be told otherwise.

Retracting this report. I grabbed a goroutine dump from an affected node and my theory turned out to be wrong.

```
goroutine 211 [select, 54886 minutes]:
k8s.io/client-go/util/certificate.(*manager).run.func1(...)
    certificate_manager.go:436 +0x229
```

The rotation goroutine is **not** stuck or missing — it is legitimately asleep inside the `select { case <-timer.C: case <-templateChanged: }`, waiting for a timer set by `sleepInterval := deadline.Sub(m.now())`. The sleep age (54886 min ≈ 38.11 d) matches kubelet uptime, so `rotate` was called once at boot, computed its deadline, entered the select, and has been waiting ever since. My "silent early return with no retry" analysis was incorrect; I missed that the outer `wait.UntilWithContext(..., rotate, time.Second)` (line 496) is a retry loop anyway, and more importantly that the goroutine simply hadn't woken up yet — it hasn't missed any wakeup.

The actual situation on the affected node:

- Cert `NotAfter` ≈ `now + 6.97d`, lifetime = 45d → `NotBefore ≈ now − 38.03d`.
- `nextRotationDeadline` returns `NotBefore + jitteryDuration(45d)`, where `jitteryDuration ∈ [0.7, 0.9) × 45d = [31.5d, 40.5d)`.
- The timer hasn't fired, so the jitter value must be ≥ 38.03/45 = **0.845**. Deadline is somewhere in the next ≤ 2.47 days, still comfortably before expiry.
- Rotation will happen on its own before the cert actually expires.

The alert I was chasing (\`KubeletServerCertificateExpiration\`, threshold < 7d) fires naturally when jitter lands in \`[0.844, 0.9)\` of the cert lifetime, because:

- EKS hard-caps \`kubernetes.io/kubelet-serving\` certs at **45 days** (per [AWS EKS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/cert-signing.html)).
- Kubelet's rotation jitter ends at \`0.9 × lifetime = 40.5d\`, i.e. a rotation wake-up as late as **4.5 days before expiry**.
- The Prometheus-operator alert threshold is **7 days**.

On a cert lifetime of ~45d, about 28% of nodes will mathematically land in \`[0.844, 0.9)\` and trip the 7-day alert even though rotation is perfectly healthy and will fire before expiry. On longer cert lifetimes (kube-controller-manager default 1 year), 0.9 × 365 = 328.5d leaves 36.5d of headroom above the 7-day threshold — not a problem. The interaction is specifically with EKS's unusually short 45-day signer lifetime.

None of this is a kubelet bug. Sorry for the noise. Closing as not planned. If someone wants to argue the jitter range should scale down for shorter cert lifetimes, or that the upstream alert threshold should be a fraction of lifetime rather than a fixed 7d, those are defensible discussions but belong in the respective component repos (kubelet / kube-prometheus-stack).

Workarounds for anyone hitting this on EKS:

1. Replace nodes before \`0.844 × lifetime\` (e.g. Karpenter \`expireAfter: 840h\` for a 45-day cert) — avoids the jitter window entirely.
2. Lower the alert threshold below \`0.1 × lifetime\` (<4.5d for EKS), or express it as a fraction of the cert lifetime.

Thanks for the patience.
