title: kubemark log dump flaking
need_summary: Whether the kubelet log metric duplication bug causing flaking is due to a race in pod status caching, anchored by the linked kubernetes/kubernetes PR 137471 and the later fix in commit 1ed5965382e09c1fdc8b363c153e9ebee0942481.
security_topic: race condition causing duplicate kubelet metrics and log dump failure
question_text:
### Which jobs are flaking?

ci-kubernetes-kubemark-100-gce

### Which tests are flaking?

DumpClusterLogs

### Since when has it been flaking?

March 6th

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-scalability-kubemark#kubemark-100&width=20

### Reason for failure (if possible)

> Error from server (InternalError): an error on the server ("An error has occurred while serving metrics:\n\ncollected metric \"kubelet_container_log_filesystem_used_bytes\" { label:{name:\"container\"  value:\"hollow-proxy\"}  label:{name:\"namespace\"  value:\"kubemark\"}  label:{name:\"pod\"  value:\"hollow-node-jlglr\"}  label:{name:\"uid\"  value:\"d43e3a5a-40c3-427c-b3b9-69a3aab282dd\"}  gauge:{value:8192}} was collected before with the same name and label values") has prevented the request from succeeding
answer_text:
The issue seems to be caused by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137471 which was merged on the day we started seeing the failures: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-kubemark-100-gce/2030165951168647168

I wrote a quick unit test and I am seeing the following race:
 1. Pod has sandbox A (READY). PLEG Relist calls GetPods(), taking a snapshot
   at time T1 that includes sandbox A.                                        
 2. Sandbox A becomes NOT_READY. SyncPod detects this with a fresh status and
   creates sandbox B (READY). This happens between T1 and when PLEG processes 
  this pod.
 3. PLEG's reconcilePodRecord calls updateCache -> GetPodStatus(ctx, pod) with
   the stale T1 snapshot. Because GetPodStatus now iterates pod.Sandboxes     
   instead of querying the CRI, it only sees sandbox A (NOT_READY) and misses
   sandbox B entirely.                                                         
 4. The pod worker reads this stale cached status. PodSandboxChanged sees no
   READY sandbox and triggers SyncPod. killPodWithSyncResult kills sandbox A
   (the only one in the stale status) but does not kill sandbox B (invisible).
   SyncPod then creates sandbox C (READY).                                     
 5. The runtime now has two READY sandboxes for the same pod: B and C.

This situation will be corrected by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1ed5965382e09c1fdc8b363c153e9ebee0942481/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/util/util.go#L45-L50 but in the meantime, kubelet will try to create metrics from two different sandboxes for the same pod which is causing the duplication issue on `kubelet_container_log_filesystem_used_bytes`.

@tallclair is this an expected behavior?

  5. The runtime now has two READY sandboxes for the same pod: B and C.

[c9] @tallclair 2026-03-25T19:02:27Z:
@dgrisonnet I'll need to dig into the code for this, but I'm confused by step 2 in your breakdown

> Sandbox A becomes NOT_READY. SyncPod detects this with a fresh status and
creates sandbox B (READY). This happens between T1 and when PLEG processes
this pod.

`SyncPod` should only ever operate on the results of the PLEG relist:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1ed5965382e09c1fdc8b363c153e9ebee0942481/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L1266-L1274

So for SyncPod to see the NOT_READY Sandbox A, the PLEG would have had to do a Relist that read the NOT_READY sandbox A. Unless I'm missing something, I don't think SyncPod can see a NOT_READY sandbox A while the pleg is still operating on a READY sandbox A.

That said, I think there's a different race condition:

1. SyncPod is running at time T0
2. PLEG global Relist starts at time T1, and reads the pod sandboxes, with none ready
3. SyncPod, still running, starts a new sandbox, Sandbox B, and finishes running (lastSyncTime=T2)
4. PLEG relist calls update status for the pod, but doesn't know about Sandbox B. It writes the cache update at time T3
5. SyncPod runs again, calls GetNewerThan with last sync time T2, and gets the pod status from step 4, since T3 > T2. However, this status is missing Sandbox B.
6. SyncPod starts a new Sandbox C

I think the issue is that the timestamp used in step 4 is _after_ the time of the relist. As long as we use the T1 timestamp in step 4, it shouldn't be a problem. I'll send a PR.

title: The pods of the StatefulSet were rebuilt during the upgrade from 1.31 to 1.34.
need_summary: Whether the StatefulSet pod rebuild caused by the missing volumeClaimTemplates.metadata.creationTimestamp field was a known issue fixed in 1.34.2, as referenced by Kubernetes PR #135087.
security_topic: StatefulSet rebuild triggered by API field removal during upgrade
question_text: We found that when Kubernetes was upgraded from 1.31 to 1.34, the pods of the StatefulSet were rebuilt. After comparing the YAML files before and after the upgrade, we found that the volumeClaimTemplates.metadata.creationTimestamp field was no longer available in version 1.34, which caused a rolling update of the StatefulSet.
answer_text: >This was resolved in 1.34.2 in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135087
thread_text:
ISSUE #137705: The pods of the StatefulSet were rebuilt during the upgrade from 1.31 to 1.34.
Author: Black-max12138
Date: 2026-03-13T07:44:55Z
Labels: kind/bug, needs-sig, needs-triage
State: closed

[c0]
### What happened?

We found that when Kubernetes was upgraded from 1.31 to 1.34, the pods of the StatefulSet were rebuilt. After comparing the YAML files before and after the upgrade, we found that the volumeClaimTemplates.metadata.creationTimestamp field was no longer available in version 1.34, which caused a rolling update of the StatefulSet.
1.31:
```
volumeClaimTemplates:
  - apiVersion: v1
    kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
    metadata:
      annotations:
        deletePolicy: retain
        name: mydata
      creationTimestamp: null
      name: mydata
    spec:
      accessModes:
      - ReadWriteOnce
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 100Gi
      storageClassName: localcsi
      volumeMode: Filesystem
```

1.34:
```
volumeClaimTemplates:
  - apiVersion: v1
    kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
    metadata:
      annotations:
        deletePolicy: retain
        name: mydata
      name: mydata
    spec:
      accessModes:
      - ReadWriteOnce
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 100Gi
      storageClassName: localcsi
      volumeMode: Filesystem
```
The **spec.volumeClaimTemplates.metadata.creationTimestamp** field is deleted.

### What did you expect to happen?

The pod of the StatefulSet is not rebuilt.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1.31 -> 1.34 upgrade

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

title: DRA scheduler plugin cannot fulfill gang scheduling with shared ResourceClaims
need_summary: Whether gang scheduling with shared ResourceClaims gets stuck because allocation must be simulated in Reserve instead of PreBind, as discussed in Kubernetes PR 136989 and PR 137647.
security_topic: scheduler deadlock with shared ResourceClaims in gang scheduling
question_text: When two Pods are created in a gang where both Pods share the same ResourceClaim, the scheduler falls into an endless loop trying to schedule the Pods and never succeeds.
answer_text:
The issue that blocks scheduling here is that the second pod cannot be scheduled until the first one goes into `PreBind` and allocate the `ResourceClaim`. Only then, the second pod can go through the scheduling cycle, but it never happens, because the first pod waits on `Permit` (before the `Binding` phase).

IIUC what we need to do is to "simulate" allocation in-memory only in `Reserve` (instead of `PreBind`), so that the second pod can pass `PreFilter` (where it's currently blocked waiting on the shared `ResourceClaim` to be allocated (in the api-server) first.

ISSUE #137617: DRA scheduler plugin cannot fulfill gang scheduling with shared ResourceClaims
Author: nojnhuh

### What happened?

When two Pods are created in a gang where both Pods share the same ResourceClaim, the scheduler falls into an endless loop trying to schedule the Pods and never succeeds.

```

### What did you expect to happen?

Both Pods schedule with the shared ResourceClaim.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a kind cluster:
```
kind build node-image --image kindest/node:latest
kind create cluster --image kindest/node:latest --config kind.yaml
```
<details>
<summary>kind.yaml</summary>

```yaml
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
nodes:
- role: control-plane
- role: worker
kubeadmConfigPatches:
  - |
    kind: ClusterConfiguration
    apiVersion: kubeadm.k8s.io/v1beta3
    apiServer:
        extraArgs:
          runtime-config: "scheduling.k8s.io/v1alpha2=true"
featureGates:
  GenericWorkload: true
  GangScheduling: true
```

</details>

Install a DRA driver:
```
helm upgrade --install dra-example-driver oci://registry.k8s.io/dra-example-driver/charts/dra-example-driver -n dra-example-driver --create-namespace

Create a ResourceClaim, PodGroup, and Pods in the PodGroup sharing the claim:

  name: single-gpu
spec:

    requests:
    - name: gpu
      exactly:
        deviceClassName: gpu.example.com
---
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1alpha2
kind: PodGroup
metadata:
  name: podgroup
spec:
  schedulingPolicy:
    gang:
      minCount: 2
---

metadata:
  name: my-app

  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: my-app
    spec:
      resourceClaims:
        - name: claim
          resourceClaimName: single-gpu
      containers:
        - name: ctr
          image: ubuntu:22.04
          command: ["bash", "-c"]
          args: ["export; trap 'exit 0' TERM; sleep 9999 & wait"]

            claims:
              - name: claim

Both Pods will schedule together if either of the following changes are made:
- Set the PodGroup's `spec.schedulingPolicy` to `basic: {}`
- Create separate ResourceClaims for each Pod instead of sharing (ResourceClaimTemplate).

comments.author: dom4ha
comments.body:
The discussion about the problem is here https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136989#discussion_r2914315596

The issue that blocks scheduling here is that the second pod cannot be scheduled until the first one goes into `PreBind` and allocate the `ResourceClaim`. Only then, the second pod can go through the scheduling cycle, but it never happens, because the first pod waits on `Permit` (before the `Binding` phase).

IIUC what we need to do is to "simulate" allocation in-memory only in `Reserve` (instead of `PreBind`), so that the second pod can pass `PreFilter` (where it's currently blocked waiting on the shared `ResourceClaim` to be allocated (in the api-server) first.

title: CVE-2026-3288: ingress-nginx rewrite-target nginx configuration injection
need_summary: Whether CVE-2026-3288 in ingress-nginx is a privilege-escalation vulnerability from creating an Ingress and what its CVSS scope/PR should be, anchored by the published CVE record and the severity-ratings.md documentation referenced by the maintainer.
security_topic: CVSS scope and required privileges for ingress-target injection vulnerability
question_text:
Hey guys,

Could you please clarify [CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H) ? If I understood correctly, to exploit this vulnerability attacker should be authenticated to Kubernetes cluster and have role with permissions to modify ingress objects.

Is it correct? If so, does it mean that attack vector (AV) should be Local and Privileges Required (PR) is High.

Thank you in advanced.

CC: @tabbysable
answer_text:
@omelnyk1 You are correct about the scope and impact of the vuln: it is a privilege escalation from "user with permission to create an ingress" to "probably cluster admin, depending on how the cluster is configured".

The difficulty you see is a constant tension with CVSS and software like Kubernetes. CVSS is best aligned with the security needs of desktop software, where there is a clear distinction between an attacker sitting at the keyboard and an attacker who is somewhere else. You will rarely see "local" attack vector in Kubernetes CVEs because local means someone who has an account on the server where the Kubernetes component is running--usually a control plane node. In the Kubernetes security model, it is discouraged and exceptionally rare for anyone other than trusted admins to have *any* access to that layer.

Similarly, in this CVE, "permissions required" is evaluated from the point of view of a cluster administrator who operates a cluster for use by engineers who run workloads on the cluster. So in this case, "none" would mean for example customers, "low" the engineers who run workloads but don't administer the cluster, and "high" the cluster administrators themselves. (This is also why you don't see many Kubernetes CVEs with high required privileges: there are not very many things that require cluster admin access and count as security vulnerabilities. Often, if a behavior is only available to cluster administrators, it's considered an ordinary bug or a dangerous feature.)

For more context on how the Security Response Committee considers these types of questions, see [our documentation on the subject](https://github.com/kubernetes/committee-security-response/blob/main/severity-ratings.md).

Author: tabbysable

[c0]
CVSS Rating: 8.8 (HIGH) [CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H)

A security issue was discovered in ingress-nginx where the nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/rewrite-target Ingress annotation can be used to inject configuration into nginx. This can lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the ingress-nginx controller, and disclosure of Secrets accessible to the controller. (Note that in the default installation, the controller can access all Secrets cluster-wide.)

### Am I vulnerable?

This issue affects ingress-nginx. If you do not have ingress-nginx installed on your cluster, you are not affected. You can check this by running `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --selector app.kubernetes.io/name=ingress-nginx`.

#### Affected Versions

- ingress-nginx: < 1.13.8
- ingress-nginx: < 1.14.4
- ingress-nginx: < 1.15.0

### How do I mitigate this vulnerability?

Prior to upgrading, this vulnerability can be mitigated by using admission control to block the use of the rewrite-target annotation.

#### How to upgrade?

To upgrade, refer to the documentation: [Upgrading Ingress-nginx](https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx/deploy/upgrade/)

### Detection

Suspicious data within the `rules.http.paths.path` field of an Ingress resource could indicate an attempt to exploit this vulnerability.

If you find evidence that this vulnerability has been exploited, please contact **security@kubernetes.io**

#### Acknowledgements

This vulnerability was reported by Kai Aizen

title: StatefulSet pod revisions not updated when MaxUnavailableStatefulSet enabled
need_summary: Whether the StatefulSet MaxUnavailable regression is fixed and safe to re-enable, with the answer anchored by Kubernetes PRs #137666 and #137904 and the 1.37 re-enable plan.
security_topic: StatefulSet update regression under MaxUnavailableStatefulSet
question_text:
The high level description of the problem is that the stateful set controller doesn't update the pods according to the latest STS revision and the pods are left crashlooping **if the first revision is faulty** and can never become available. This doesn't happen if the `MaxUnavailableStatefulSet` feature is disabled.

Unfortunately I cannot create a much simpler example, but I attach the relevant controller log messages below.

Based on these logs you can see that:

1. The Stackable Operator for Trino (`trino-op` from now on) creates two `StatefulSet` objects with a single replica. They both expose the same problem, so for simplicity, I will use only one of them from now on (`trino-coordinator-default`).
2. The initial revision of this sts is `trino-coordinator-default-5f5598d4c8`. This first STS  revision has a faulty command args  and can never become available.
3. The `trino-op` updates the sts rapidly to the revision `trino-coordinator-default-787556ff59`. Now the STS command args are correct and the pods should be able to become ready.
4. The pod created initially is never updated so it never becomes ready.

To summarize my understanding, the sts revision is never updated if the pod never becomes ready, and the pod doesn't become ready because it has an old revision.
answer_text:
Got the most minimal reproducer. The main part is the `.spec.podManagementPolicy`. This problem happens ONLY for `Parallel`, which is expected to recover a pod. Here's a simple StatefulSet with a Service:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: sts
spec:
  replicas: 1
  podManagementPolicy: Parallel
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      baz: blah
      foo: bar
  serviceName: svc
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        baz: blah
        foo: bar
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: webserver
        args:
        - test-webserver1
        image: registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/agnhost:2.55
  updateStrategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: svc
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  clusterIPs:
  - None
  internalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
  ipFamilies:
  - IPv4
  ipFamilyPolicy: SingleStack
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 80
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: 80
  selector:
    baz: blah
    foo: bar
  sessionAffinity: None
  type: ClusterIP
```
Now you can trigger the problem running `kubectl apply -f test-sts.yaml ; sed -i "s/test-webserver1/test-webserver/g" test-sts.yaml; sleep 3 ; kubectl apply -f test-sts.yaml`. With k8s 1.34.3 this will recover correctly, with 1.35.0 (I'm using kind locally), it does not. 

So the fix is to take into account pod management policy during calculating unavailable pods.

### What happened?

I decided to open this issue after investigating https://github.com/stackabletech/trino-operator/issues/854.

The high level description of the problem is that the stateful set controller doesn't update the pods according to the latest STS revision and the pods are left crashlooping **if the first revision is faulty** and can never become available. This doesn't happen if the `MaxUnavailableStatefulSet` feature is disabled.

Unfortunately I cannot create a much simpler example, but I attach the relevant controller log messages below.

Based on these logs you can see that:

1. The Stackable Operator for Trino (`trino-op` from now on) creates two `StatefulSet` objects with a single replica. They both expose the same problem, so for simplicity, I will use only one of them from now on (`trino-coordinator-default`).
2. The initial revision of this sts is `trino-coordinator-default-5f5598d4c8`. This first STS  revision has a faulty command args  and can never become available.
3. The `trino-op` updates the sts rapidly to the revision `trino-coordinator-default-787556ff59`. Now the STS command args are correct and the pods should be able to become ready.
4. The pod created initially is never updated so it never becomes ready.

To summarize my understanding, the sts revision is never updated if the pod never becomes ready, and the pod doesn't become ready because it has an old revision.

The pod should become ready according to the `updateRevision` of the sts.

@@ -772,21 +772,26 @@ func updateStatefulSetAfterInvariantEstablished(ctx context.Context, ssc *defaul
 	}

-	if unavailablePods >= maxUnavailable {

-			logger.V(4).Info("StatefulSet found unavailablePods, more than the allowed maxUnavailable",
-				"statefulSet", klog.KObj(set),
-				"unavailablePods", unavailablePods,
-				"maxUnavailable", maxUnavailable)
-		}
+	logger.V(4).Info("StatefulSet update checking for unavailable Pods",
+		"statefulSet", klog.KObj(set),
+		"unavailablePods", unavailablePods,
+		"maxUnavailable", maxUnavailable)
 
-		return &status, nil
+	if unavailablePods > maxUnavailable {
+		logger.V(2).Info("StatefulSet found unavailablePods, more than the allowed maxUnavailable",
+			"statefulSet", klog.KObj(set),
+			"unavailablePods", unavailablePods,
+			"maxUnavailable", maxUnavailable)
 	}
 
 	// Now we need to delete MaxUnavailable- unavailablePods
 	// start deleting one by one starting from the highest ordinal first
+	// For STSs with only one replica, we should delete the pod if it is unavailable,
+	// even if maxUnavailable is 1, to make progress.
 	podsToDelete := maxUnavailable - unavailablePods
+	if unavailablePods == 1 && maxUnavailable == 1 {
+		podsToDelete = 1
+	}
 
 	deletedPods := 0
 	for target := len(replicas) - 1; target >= updateMin && deletedPods < podsToDelete; target-- {

### What happened?

I decided to open this issue after investigating https://github.com/stackabletech/trino-operator/issues/854.

The high level description of the problem is that the stateful set controller doesn't update the pods according to the latest STS revision and the pods are left crashlooping **if the first revision is faulty** and can never become available. This doesn't happen if the `MaxUnavailableStatefulSet` feature is disabled.

Unfortunately I cannot create a much simpler example, but I attach the relevant controller log messages below.

Based on these logs you can see that:

1. The Stackable Operator for Trino (`trino-op` from now on) creates two `StatefulSet` objects with a single replica. They both expose the same problem, so for simplicity, I will use only one of them from now on (`trino-coordinator-default`).
2. The initial revision of this sts is `trino-coordinator-default-5f5598d4c8`. This first STS  revision has a faulty command args  and can never become available.
3. The `trino-op` updates the sts rapidly to the revision `trino-coordinator-default-787556ff59`. Now the STS command args are correct and the pods should be able to become ready.
4. The pod created initially is never updated so it never becomes ready.

To summarize my understanding, the sts revision is never updated if the pod never becomes ready, and the pod doesn't become ready because it has an old revision.

In the logs you see that `currentRevision` is never the same as `updateRevision`:

```
I0304 15: 25:06.514308       1 stateful_set_control.go: 146]"StatefulSet revisions" statefulSet = "kuttl-test-distinct-turtle/trino-coordinator-default" currentRevision = "trino-coordinator-default-5f5598d4c8" updateRevision = "trino-coordinator-default-787556ff59"
```

### What did you expect to happen?

The pod should become ready according to the `updateRevision` of the sts.
Again, this was indeed the case until `MaxUnavailableStatefulSet` feature gate was enabled.

I can reproduce this bug using the `trino-op` but unfortunately I don't have a minimal example.

comments.author: razvan
comments.body:
I'm not sure if this is the correct fix, but the patch below solves the problem for us.

The problem was two fold:

1. The pods are not updated when unavailablePods==maxUnavailable but they can also never become available in that revision.
2. Seems there is a corner case when the STS only has one replica, in which case the Pod is also not updated.

```diff
diff --git a/pkg/controller/statefulset/stateful_set_control.go b/pkg/controller/statefulset/stateful_set_control.go
index dd339cc7814..94eef25cb8d 100644
--- a/pkg/controller/statefulset/stateful_set_control.go
+++ b/pkg/controller/statefulset/stateful_set_control.go
@@ -772,21 +772,26 @@ func updateStatefulSetAfterInvariantEstablished(ctx context.Context, ssc *defaul
 	}
 	metrics.UnavailableReplicas.WithLabelValues(set.Namespace, set.Name, podManagementPolicy).Set(float64(unavailablePods))
 
-	if unavailablePods >= maxUnavailable {
-		// log only when a true violation occurs.
-		if unavailablePods > maxUnavailable {
-			logger.V(4).Info("StatefulSet found unavailablePods, more than the allowed maxUnavailable",
-				"statefulSet", klog.KObj(set),
-				"unavailablePods", unavailablePods,
-				"maxUnavailable", maxUnavailable)
-		}
+	logger.V(4).Info("StatefulSet update checking for unavailable Pods",
+		"statefulSet", klog.KObj(set),
+		"unavailablePods", unavailablePods,
+		"maxUnavailable", maxUnavailable)
 
-		return &status, nil
+	if unavailablePods > maxUnavailable {
+		logger.V(2).Info("StatefulSet found unavailablePods, more than the allowed maxUnavailable",
+			"statefulSet", klog.KObj(set),
+			"unavailablePods", unavailablePods,
+			"maxUnavailable", maxUnavailable)
 	}
 
 	// Now we need to delete MaxUnavailable- unavailablePods
 	// start deleting one by one starting from the highest ordinal first
+	// For STSs with only one replica, we should delete the pod if it is unavailable,
+	// even if maxUnavailable is 1, to make progress.
 	podsToDelete := maxUnavailable - unavailablePods
+	if unavailablePods == 1 && maxUnavailable == 1 {
+		podsToDelete = 1
+	}
 
 	deletedPods := 0
 	for target := len(replicas) - 1; target >= updateMin && deletedPods < podsToDelete; target-- {
```

comments.author: soltysh
comments.body:
Got the most minimal reproducer. The main part is the `.spec.podManagementPolicy`. This problem happens ONLY for `Parallel`, which is expected to recover a pod. Here's a simple StatefulSet with a Service:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: sts
spec:
  replicas: 1
  podManagementPolicy: Parallel
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      baz: blah
      foo: bar
  serviceName: svc
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        baz: blah
        foo: bar
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: webserver
        args:
        - test-webserver1
        image: registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/agnhost:2.55
  updateStrategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: svc
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  clusterIPs:
  - None
  internalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
  ipFamilies:
  - IPv4
  ipFamilyPolicy: SingleStack
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 80
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: 80
  selector:
    baz: blah
    foo: bar
  sessionAffinity: None
  type: ClusterIP
```
Now you can trigger the problem running `kubectl apply -f test-sts.yaml ; sed -i "s/test-webserver1/test-webserver/g" test-sts.yaml; sleep 3 ; kubectl apply -f test-sts.yaml`. With k8s 1.34.3 this will recover correctly, with 1.35.0 (I'm using kind locally), it does not. 

So the fix is to take into account pod management policy during calculating unavailable pods.

title: Windows: Seeing intermittent DNS issues on k8s > 1.30
need_summary: Whether the intermittent Windows DNS/network failure was caused by stale duplicate HNS endpoints and what fix in Kubernetes pull request 138000 addressed it.
security_topic: stale HNS remote endpoint causing intermittent DNS/network failure on Windows pods
question_text:
When operating in environments with high pod churn rates—where pods are frequently created and terminated—and multiple services are configured to reference a single deployment, we observed that network connectivity on some of the pods is failing on windows nodes.

On the pods where we have network issue, tried to do DNS lookup by exec into the pods and it failed to resolve the DNS.
answer_text:
Your observation looks correct. A stale remote endpoint is causing VFP to prefer the remote endpoint’s MAC address over the local one, which results in packets being encapsulated and sent to a different node.

I’ve implemented a fix to prevent multiple endpoints from existing with the same IP (shared over slack). It would be really helpful if you could test this using the shared kube-proxy binary. The changes are based on the 1.33 release, since your testing was also done on that version.

comments.body:
### What happened?

When operating in environments with high pod churn rates—where pods are frequently created and terminated—and multiple services are configured to reference a single deployment, we observed that network connectivity on some of the pods is failing on windows nodes.

On the pods where we have network issue, tried to do DNS lookup by exec into the pods and it failed to resolve the DNS.

Attached are the logs on two windows nodes

[9a98.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25727718/9a98.zip)

[bf83.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25727725/bf83.zip)

### What did you expect to happen?

Network connectivity shouldn't break on windows pods and DNS resolution should succeed.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1.  Deploy kubernetes cluster with limited available IPs for pods on both Linux and Windows node.
2. Deploy Linux pods that consume almost all IPs.
3. Deploy service type LoadBalancer that refer to Linux pods, This will trigger kube-proxy to create Remote HNS endpoint on Windows. This Remote HNS endpoint will have Linux pod IP.
4. Scale down the Linux pods to 1.
5. Do multiple time scaling up and down.
6. Deploy windows deployment with multiple replicas and have multiple service referencing the deployment.
7. Scale down the windows pods to 1.
8. Perform the same operation multiple time (scaling up and down)
9. After few days we see that on few of the pods, if we do the nslookup, it fails to connect and resolve DNS.

### Anything else we need to know?

I was going through the below PR and want to check whether any regression caused the network connectivity issue. 
PR1: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135146
PR2: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133953
All our customers reported that, they are seeing intermittent network connectivity issues on K8S >1.30.

>... absent evidence that they did cause a regression ... Have you contacted EKS support? Flaky networking issues may not be related to any bugs in Kubernetes, and this is not a general support forum. (we have e.g. https://discuss.kubernetes.io/)

I raised this issue as I was not able to figure out whether any of the PR's caused networking changes and to get inputs on it.

Based on my review, none of the PRs you mentioned appear to be the cause of this regression. [PR1 ](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135146) was not backported to 1.31, and since the issue is occurring on 1.31 as well, it is unlikely to be related. [PR2 ](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133953) was backported to 1.31, but its changes do not impact LoadBalancer creation.

From the logs you shared, I can see that DNS HNS policies are present on both nodes. However, one difference I noticed is that the DSR flag does not appear to be set in the logs. This could potentially be the reason for the issue, as it may prevent the VFP load balancer rules from being installed.

Additionally, the logs you shared did not include kubeclusterconfig.json or kubeproxy error logs. I suspect that in the newer release deployments, one of the required flags may not have been set. In particular:

`--enable-dsr="true"` (while starting Windows kube-proxy)

`--feature-gates="WinDSR=true,WinOverlay=false"` (configured in kubeclusterconfig.json)

comments.author: princepereira
comments.body:
@smandhada16 ,

Based on the details you shared, there are two CoreDNS pods: 192.168.7.38 (coredns-6b7fdfbc95-zfhv2) and 192.168.7.62 (coredns-6b7fdfbc95-4v4n9). These same pods are also configured as backend DIPs in the HNS policy as well as in the VFP load balancer rules.
Since the expected DNS IP addresses are correctly configured in the HNS policies and VFP rules that you shared, we can reasonably exclude the earlier suspected PRs as the root cause.

When the VFP port performs backend selection for DNS queries, some requests are directed to 192.168.7.38, while others are routed to 192.168.7.62. From the observations so far, DNS queries sent to 192.168.7.38 are consistently resolved and return valid responses. However, queries that are routed to 192.168.7.62 appear to leave the node but do not receive a response afterward. This could potentially indicate an issue either with the network path or with the DNS pod itself.

The intermittent DNS success you are observing likely corresponds to cases where the backend selection routes the request to 192.168.7.38, while the failures occur when 192.168.7.62 is selected as the backend.

@smandhada16 ,

Your observation looks correct. A stale remote endpoint is causing VFP to prefer the remote endpoint’s MAC address over the local one, which results in packets being encapsulated and sent to a different node.

I’ve implemented a fix to prevent multiple endpoints from existing with the same IP (shared over slack). It would be really helpful if you could test this using the shared kube-proxy binary. The changes are based on the 1.33 release, since your testing was also done on that version.

Thanks,

title: Flaking TestDRA/all/ControllerManagerMetrics
need_summary: Whether the nil-pointer panic in dynamicresources.go is caused by binding-condition handling and requires a client-side check before updating the allocation result, anchored by the cited Kubernetes validation code and file/line references.
security_topic: nil-pointer panic in dynamic resource claim binding
question_text:
The panic in `dynamicresources.go:1247` is probably the allocation result:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b9e0f9d10ae94665d6fc1817f7310672a905ffd0/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/dynamicresources/dynamicresources.go#L1247

I think what happens is that the claims gets deallocated while a new pod is about to be added to the `ReservedFor`. `PreBind` should check for that, but doesn't.

I'm still not sure why the controller deallocates, though. That part is still a bit odd.
answer_text:
It didn't need to: server-side validation rejects a status with non-nil `ReservedFor` and nil `Allocation`:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b9e0f9d10ae94665d6fc1817f7310672a905ffd0/pkg/apis/resource/validation/validation.go#L439-L441

The panic is limited to configurations where binding conditions are enabled. Because of that new code, the client now needs to check before updating the allocation result.

comments.author: pohly
comments.body:
> PreBind should check for that, but doesn't.

It didn't need to: server-side validation rejects a status with non-nil `ReservedFor` and nil `Allocation`:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b9e0f9d10ae94665d6fc1817f7310672a905ffd0/pkg/apis/resource/validation/validation.go#L439-L441

The panic is limited to configurations where binding conditions are enabled. Because of that new code, the client now needs to check before updating the allocation result.

title: kube-apiserver removes all managedFields if conversion webhook is not available

question_text:
I would expect to get an error back from the apiserver in cases like this.

thread_text:
ISSUE #136919: kube-apiserver removes all managedFields if conversion webhook is not available
Author: sbueringer
Date: 2026-02-10T19:19:17Z
Labels: kind/bug, needs-sig, needs-triage
State: closed

[c0]
### What happened?

The apiserver removes all managedFields of an object under the following circumstances:
* object has managedField entries of multiple apiVersions
* conversion webhook is (potentially temporarily) not available/reachable
* there's a write on the object (via label, or client-side apply, SSA just returns an appropriate error, more details below)

### What did you expect to happen?

I would expect to get an error back from the apiserver in cases like this.
Removing all managedFields can have a big impact on the results of subsequent writes.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Required files:
[cr_cluster.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25218546/cr_cluster.yaml)
[cr_cluster_ssa.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25218545/cr_cluster_ssa.yaml)
[crd_cluster.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25218548/crd_cluster.yaml)
[crd_cluster_no_conversion.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25218547/crd_cluster_no_conversion.yaml)

Create a kind cluster (I was using kindest/node:v1.35.0)
```bash
kind create cluster
```

Deploy the CRD (without conversion configured for now so we are able to prepare managedFields with v1beta1 & v1beta2)
```bash
kubectl apply -f ./crd_cluster_no_conversion.yaml
```

Deploy and prepare the cluster
```bash
kubectl apply -f ./cr_cluster.yaml
kubectl label clusters.v1beta1.cluster.x-k8s.io cluster-1  def=ghi --overwrite
kubectl label clusters.v1beta2.cluster.x-k8s.io cluster-1  abc=def --overwrite
kubectl get cluster cluster-1 -o json --show-managed-fields | jq '.metadata.managedFields' | grep apiVersion
```

Update the CRD to configure an unreachable conversion webhook
```bash
kubectl apply -f ./crd_cluster.yaml
```

Try to update the cluster with SSA:
```
kubectl apply -f ./cr_cluster_ssa.yaml --server-side --field-manager=kubectl-ssa-test --show-managed-fields -o yaml
```
Output
```
Error from server: conversion webhook for cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2, Kind=Cluster failed: Post "https://webhook-service.system.svc:443/convert?timeout=30s": service "webhook-service" not found
```

```
kubectl apply -f ./cr_cluster_ssa.yaml --show-managed-fields -o yaml
```
Output (managedFields are gone)

```
Output
```

[c3] @jpbetz 2026-02-10T19:50:26Z:
The code the drops the managedFields is:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f42571572d241a2cdeffa3962c0ccf1f59180113/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/managedfields/internal/fieldmanager.go#L160

If we instead preserve the managedFields here from the live object the specific update's field changes won't be tracked, but at least the existing field ownership data will be preserved.

I fix along the lines of:

```diff
  func (f *FieldManager) UpdateNoErrors(liveObj, newObj runtime.Object, manager string) runtime.Object {
      obj, err := f.Update(liveObj, newObj, manager)
      if err != nil {
          atMostEverySecond.Do(func() {
              ns, name := "unknown", "unknown"
              if accessor, err := meta.Accessor(newObj); err == nil {
                  ns = accessor.GetNamespace()
                  name = accessor.GetName()
              }
              klog.ErrorS(err, "[SHOULD NOT HAPPEN] failed to update managedFields", "versionKind",
                  newObj.GetObjectKind().GroupVersionKind(), "namespace", ns, "name", name)
          })
+          // Preserve the managedFields from the live object rather than
+          // stripping them entirely, to avoid silent data loss when the
+          // managedFields update fails (e.g. due to an unavailable
+          // conversion webhook).
+          if liveAccessor, err := meta.Accessor(liveObj); err == nil {
+              if newAccessor, err := meta.Accessor(newObj); err == nil {
+                  newAccessor.SetManagedFields(liveAccessor.GetManagedFields())
+                  return newObj
+              }
+          }
          // Fall back to removing managedFields if we can't access the live object.
          RemoveObjectManagedFields(newObj)
          return newObj
      }
      return obj
  }
```

This fix would preserve the existing managed fields, which is I think the best option given that the conversion webhook is unavailable.

title: Some crashed or OOMKilled containers fail to restart in v1.35
need_summary: Whether the kubelet restart-related container restart bug in v1.35 is fixed by the referenced commit 237996ca0ec076c5a149c7341d434b680c695720 and needs cherry-picking back to 1.35.
security_topic: container restart failure after kubelet restart
question_text:
After upgrading Kubernetes from v1.34.2 to v1.35.0, we observed a scenario where a pod with multiple containers does not restart a crashed application container, leaving the pod in an Error state indefinitely.

This behavior was not observed on v1.34.2. Reverting the kubelet back to v1.34.2 causes the issue to disappear.

**Observed Behavior:**
The main container terminates but never restarts:
```
State:          Terminated
  Reason:       Error
  Exit Code:    2
  Started:      Tue, 27 Jan 2026 16:11:01 +0000
  Finished:     Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:08:55 +0000
  Ready:      False
  Restart Count:  0
```

The sidecar container continues to run normally:
```
State:          Running
Started:        Tue, 27 Jan 2026 16:10:54 +0000
Ready:          True
Restart Count:  0
```

Pod conditions show:
```
Conditions:
  Type                        Status
  PodReadyToStartContainers   True
  Initialized                 True
  Ready                       False
  ContainersReady              False
  PodScheduled                True
```

No useful logs or errors appear in `kubectl describe pod` output, events, or `kubelet` logs.

**Notes:**
- This issue seems to only affect pods with more than one container
- We are unsure whether it's just pods with an `initContainer` or does it also apply to `container` sidecars
- Manually killing the process in the sidecar container or deleting the pod helps getting it back to working state
- `RestartAllContainersOnContainerExits` is not enabled

**Possibly related?**
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134345

### What did you expect to happen?

Containers should reliably restart every time they crash.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The best way we found to reproduce this is by running a pod with 2 containers: an initContainer with `restartPolicy: Always` and an application container that we manually crash with `kill 1` command.
It might not work right first time, but we managed to reproduce this multiple times getting pods stuck in Error state that they never recover from automatically.
answer_text:
We confirmed that behaviour presented **after a Kubelet restart**. We were able to consistently reproduce it by restarting Kubelet and then force exiting the main container with `kill 1`. It would remain Completed 1/2.

We also built Kubelet from this commit: https://github.com/george-angel/kubernetes/commit/237996ca0ec076c5a149c7341d434b680c695720 and can confirm this fixes the behaviour described. Restarting the kubelet and issueing `kill 1` on the main container, correctly restarts it.

Thats not to say its a complete fix, but it does address the behaviour described in the issue.

title: kubelet nodeinfomanager does not reconcile CSINode ownerReference when Node is replaced with same name but different UID, leading to GC deletion
need_summary: Whether the CSINode ownerReference UID mismatch bug is already fixed in Kubernetes, based on pull request https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/131098 and the note that it is fixed in v1.35 but not backported.
security_topic: CSINode ownerReference stale-UID garbage-collection bug
question_text:
When kubelet registers a CSI driver via tryUpdateCSINode in nodeinfomanager.go, and a CSINode object already exists for the node, kubelet should verify that the existing CSINode's ownerReference UID matches the current Node object's UID.

If the UIDs do not match (e.g., the Node was replaced with the same name but a new UID), kubelet should either:
* Delete the stale CSINode and recreate it with the correct ownerReference, or
* Update the existing CSINode's ownerReference to reflect the current Node UID

This would prevent the garbage collector from deleting a CSINode that was just successfully updated with valid driver registration info, simply because it still carried a stale ownerReference pointing to a previous Node UID that no longer exists.

This is the same class of bug that was identified and fixed for Lease objects in #109777.
answer_text:
Didn't we fix this in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/131098 ?

In fact I am pretty sure that, this issue should be fixed in v1.35, but we have not backported this fix to older versions of kube, so you may be running into that.
thread_text:
ISSUE #136899: kubelet nodeinfomanager does not reconcile CSINode ownerReference when Node is replaced with same name but different UID, leading to GC deletion Author: rajeeshckr Date: 2026-02-10T05:26:45Z Labels: kind/bug, needs-sig, needs-triage State: closed [c0] ### What happened? In our cluster, the node with same name got recreated, hence it should have the CSINode already there. notice kubelet start at `16:23:07.906` But, the GC collection of the CSINode happened after the new node was launched notice GC at `16:24:03.591`, that was done for instance ID `i-019f660891131cc51` When the kubelet on the new node started up, it failed to do any updates on CSINode making it eligible for GC shown above ### What did you expect to happen? When kubelet registers a CSI driver via tryUpdateCSINode in nodeinfomanager.go, and a CSINode object already exists for the node, kubelet should verify that the existing CSINode's ownerReference UID matches the current Node object's UID. If the UIDs do not match (e.g., the Node was replaced with the same name but a new UID), kubelet should either: * Delete the stale CSINode and recreate it with the correct ownerReference, or * Update the existing CSINode's ownerReference to reflect the current Node UID This would prevent the garbage collector from deleting a CSINode that was just successfully updated with valid driver registration info, simply because it still carried a stale ownerReference pointing to a previous Node UID that no longer exists. This is the same class of bug that was identified and fixed for Lease objects in #109777. ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? This is a race condition that depends on GC timing relative to CSI driver registration. In the normal case, GC deletes the stale CSINode before the new kubelet's CSI driver registers, so tryUpdateCSINode takes the CreateCSINode() path and everything works. The bug manifests when GC is delayed. Theoretical steps to reproduce: ``` # 1. Identify your node name NODE_NAME=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') # 2. Record the current Node UID and CSINode ownerReference UID (should match) echo "Node UID: $(kubectl get node $NODE_NAME -o jsonpath='{.metadata.uid}')" echo "CSINode ref: $(kubectl get csinode $NODE_NAME -o jsonpath='{.metadata.ownerReferences[0].uid}')" # 3. Delete the Node object (kubelet will re-register it automatically with a new UID) kubectl delete node $NODE_NAME # 4. Wait for the node to re-register kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node/$NODE_NAME --timeout=120s # 5. Compare UIDs again — they will NOT match echo "New Node UID: $(kubectl get node $NODE_NAME -o jsonpath='{.metadata.uid}')" echo "CSINode ownerRef UID: $(kubectl get csinode $NODE_NAME -o jsonpath='{.metadata.ownerReferences[0].uid}')" # 6. Wait for garbage collector to delete the stale CSINode (~30-60 seconds) echo "Waiting for GC to delete CSINode..." while kubectl get csinode $NODE_NAME &>/dev/null; do sleep 5 echo "CSINode still exists, waiting..." done echo "CSINode deleted by garbage collector" # 7. Confirm CSINode is gone and does not come back sleep 30 kubectl get csinode $NODE_NAME # Expected: Error from server (NotFound): csinodes.storage.k8s.io "" not found # 8. Create a PVC and pod to demonstrate the impact kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF' apiVersion: v1 kind: PersistentVolumeClaim metadata: name: csinode-repro-pvc spec: accessModes: - ReadWriteOnce resources: requests: storage: 1Gi --- apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: csinode-repro-pod spec: nodeName: NODE_NAME_PLACEHOLDER containers: - name: app image: busybox command: ["sleep", "3600"] volumeMounts: - name: data mountPath: /data volumes: - name: data persistentVolumeClaim: claimName: csinode-repro-pvc EOF # Patch in the actual node name kubectl patch pod csinode-repro-pod --type=json \ -p="[{\"op\":\"replace\",\"path\":\"/spec/nodeName\",\"value\":\"$NODE_NAME\"}]" 2>/dev/null || true # 9. Observe the volume attachment failure kubectl describe pod csinode-repro-pod | grep -A5 "Events" # Expected: # Warning FailedAttachVolume attachdetach-controller # AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "pvc-xxx" : # csinode.storage.k8s.io "" not found # 10. Cleanup kubectl delete pod csinode-repro-pod --force --grace-period=0 2>/dev/null kubectl delete pvc csinode-repro-pvc 2>/dev/null ``` ### Anything else we need to know? _No response_ ### Kubernetes version
```console $ kubectl version "Kubelet version" kubeletVersion="v1.33.4" ```

AWS

title: CVE-2025-15566: ingress-nginx auth-proxy-set-headers nginx configuration injection
need_summary: Whether CVE-2025-15566 in ingress-nginx allows nginx configuration injection leading to code execution and secret disclosure, anchored by the official CVE feed and the fixed versions v1.12.5 and v1.13.1.
security_topic: mitigation and fixed versions for nginx configuration injection

thread_text:
ISSUE #136789: CVE-2025-15566: ingress-nginx auth-proxy-set-headers nginx configuration injection
Author: tabbysable
Date: 2026-02-06T02:54:24Z
Labels: kind/bug, sig/network, area/security, committee/security-response, triage/accepted, official-cve-feed
State: closed

[c0]
CVSS Rating: [CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H)

A security issue was discovered in ingress-nginx where the nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-proxy-set-headers Ingress annotation can be used to inject configuration into nginx. This can lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the ingress-nginx controller, and disclosure of Secrets accessible to the controller. (Note that in the default installation, the controller can access all Secrets cluster-wide.)

### Am I vulnerable?

This issue affects ingress-nginx. If you do not have ingress-nginx installed on your cluster, you are not affected. You can check this by running `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --selector app.kubernetes.io/name=ingress-nginx`.

#### Affected Versions

- ingress-nginx: < v1.12.5
- ingress-nginx: < v1.13.1

### How do I mitigate this vulnerability?

ACTION REQUIRED: The following steps must be taken to mitigate this vulnerability: Upgrade ingress-nginx to v1.12.5, v1.13.1, or any later version.

#### How to upgrade?

To upgrade, refer to the documentation: [Upgrading Ingress-nginx](https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx/deploy/upgrade/)

### Detection

Suspicious data within a configmap passed to the `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-proxy-set-headers` annotation of an Ingress resource could indicate an attempt to exploit this vulnerability.

If you find evidence that this vulnerability has been exploited, please contact **security@kubernetes.io**

#### Acknowledgements

This issue was discovered **and patched** by Jan-Otto Kröpke.

ISSUE #136680: CVE-2026-24514: ingress-nginx Admission Controller denial of service
Author: tabbysable
Date: 2026-02-02T03:06:14Z
Labels: kind/bug, sig/network, area/security, lifecycle/frozen, committee/security-response, triage/accepted, official-cve-feed
State: closed

[c0]
CVSS Rating: [CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H)

A security issue was discovered in [ingress-nginx](https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx) where the validating admission controller feature is subject to a denial of service condition. By sending large requests to the validating admission controller, an attacker can cause memory consumption, which may result in the ingress-nginx controller pod being killed or the node running out of memory.

### Am I vulnerable?

* This issue affects ingress-nginx. If you do not have ingress-nginx installed on your cluster, you are not affected. You can check this by running \`kubectl get pods \--all-namespaces \--selector [app.kubernetes.io/name=ingress-nginx](http://app.kubernetes.io/name=ingress-nginx)\`.

#### Affected Versions

- ingress-nginx: < 1.13.7
- ingress-nginx: < 1.14.3

### How do I mitigate this vulnerability?

ACTION REQUIRED: The following steps must be taken to mitigate this vulnerability: Upgrade ingress-nginx to v1.13.7, v1.14.3, or any later version.

#### How to upgrade?

To upgrade, refer to the documentation: [Upgrading Ingress-nginx](https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx/deploy/upgrade/)

### Detection

Requests larger than a few megabytes being sent to the ingress-nginx admission controller may indicate an attempt to exploit this vulnerability.

### Acknowledgements

This issue was discovered by Matan Shabtay.
The issue was fixed and coordinated by Steven Jin, Marco Ebert, and Tabitha Sable

If you find evidence that this vulnerability has been exploited, please contact **security@kubernetes.io**

need_summary: Whether the ingress-nginx auth-url protection bypass is real and what versions fix it, anchored by CVE-2026-24513 and the documented fixed versions 1.13.7 and 1.14.3.
security_topic: auth-url protection bypass under custom-errors misconfiguration
question_text: How do I mitigate this vulnerability?
answer_text:
ACTION REQUIRED: The following steps must be taken to mitigate this vulnerability: Upgrade ingress-nginx to v1.13.7, v1.14.3, or any later version.

Prior to upgrading, this vulnerability can be mitigated by checking to confirm your custom errors backend correctly respects the `X-Code` HTTP header.
thread_text:
ISSUE #136679: CVE-2026-24513: ingress-nginx auth-url protection bypass
Author: tabbysable
Date: 2026-02-02T03:06:04Z
Labels: kind/bug, sig/network, area/security, lifecycle/frozen, committee/security-response, triage/accepted, official-cve-feed
State: closed

[c0]
CVSS Rating: [CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)

A security issue was discovered in [ingress-nginx](https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx) where the protection afforded by the `auth-url` Ingress annotation may not be effective in the presence of a specific misconfiguration.

If the ingress-nginx controller is configured with a default custom-errors configuration that includes HTTP errors 401 or 403, and if the configured default custom-errors backend is defective and fails to respect the X-Code HTTP header, then an Ingress with the `auth-url` annotation may be accessed even when authentication fails.

Note that the built-in custom-errors backend works correctly. To trigger this issue requires an administrator to specifically configure ingress-nginx with a broken external component.

### Am I vulnerable?

* This issue affects ingress-nginx. If you do not have ingress-nginx installed on your cluster, you are not affected. You can check this by running \`kubectl get pods \--all-namespaces \--selector [app.kubernetes.io/name=ingress-nginx](http://app.kubernetes.io/name=ingress-nginx)\`.
* This issue only affects Ingresses using the `auth-url` annotation. If you are not adding authentication to your Ingresses using the `auth-url` annotation, then you are not at risk.
* This issue only affects ingress-nginx controllers that have been configured with default custom-errors settings via editing the controller command-line arguments and configuration map. If you are using per-Ingress custom-errors set via Ingress annotations, then you are not at risk.

#### Affected Versions

- ingress-nginx: < 1.13.7
- ingress-nginx: < 1.14.3

### How do I mitigate this vulnerability?

ACTION REQUIRED: The following steps must be taken to mitigate this vulnerability: Upgrade ingress-nginx to v1.13.7, v1.14.3, or any later version.

Prior to upgrading, this vulnerability can be mitigated by checking to confirm your custom errors backend correctly respects the `X-Code` HTTP header.

#### How to upgrade?

To upgrade, refer to the documentation: [Upgrading Ingress-nginx](https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx/deploy/upgrade/)

### Detection

If you are able to load a URL protected by the `auth-url` annotation despite failing authentication, then you are affected by this vulnerability.

### Acknowledgements
This issue was discovered by Aurelia Schittler.
The issue was fixed and coordinated by Tabitha Sable and Marco Ebert.

If you find evidence that this vulnerability has been exploited, please contact **security@kubernetes.io**

title: CVE-2026-24512: ingress-nginx rules.http.paths.path nginx configuration injection
need_summary: Whether CVE-2026-24512 in ingress-nginx is exploitable via rules.http.paths.path nginx configuration injection, and the answer anchors on the CVE entry plus the fixed versions v1.13.7 and v1.14.3 and mitigation guidance.
security_topic: applicability and mitigation for nginx config injection vulnerability
question_text:
### Am I vulnerable?

This issue affects ingress-nginx. If you do not have ingress-nginx installed on your cluster, you are not affected. You can check this by running `kubectl get pods \--all-namespaces \--selector app.kubernetes.io/name=ingress-nginx`.
answer_text:
ACTION REQUIRED: The following steps must be taken to mitigate this vulnerability: Upgrade ingress-nginx to v1.13.7, v1.14.3, or any later version.

Prior to upgrading, this vulnerability can be mitigated by using a validating admission controller to reject Ingress resources with the `ImplementationSpecific` path type.
thread_text:
ISSUE #136678: CVE-2026-24512: ingress-nginx rules.http.paths.path nginx configuration injection
Author: tabbysable
Date: 2026-02-02T03:05:54Z
Labels: kind/bug, sig/network, area/security, lifecycle/frozen, committee/security-response, triage/accepted, official-cve-feed
State: closed

[c0]
CVSS Rating: [CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H)

A security issue was discovered in [ingress-nginx](https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx) where the `rules.http.paths.path` Ingress field can be used to inject configuration into nginx. This can lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the ingress-nginx controller, and disclosure of Secrets accessible to the controller. (Note that in the default installation, the controller can access all Secrets cluster-wide.)

### Am I vulnerable?

This issue affects ingress-nginx. If you do not have ingress-nginx installed on your cluster, you are not affected. You can check this by running \`kubectl get pods \--all-namespaces \--selector app.kubernetes.io/name=ingress-nginx\`.

#### Affected Versions

- ingress-nginx: < v1.13.7
- ingress-nginx: < v1.14.3

### How do I mitigate this vulnerability?

ACTION REQUIRED: The following steps must be taken to mitigate this vulnerability: Upgrade ingress-nginx to v1.13.7, v1.14.3, or any later version.

Prior to upgrading, this vulnerability can be mitigated by using a validating admission controller to reject Ingress resources with the `ImplementationSpecific` path type.

#### How to upgrade?

To upgrade, refer to the documentation: [Upgrading Ingress-nginx](https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx/deploy/upgrade/)

### Detection

Suspicious data within the rules.http.paths.path field of an Ingress resource could indicate an attempt to exploit this vulnerability.

### Acknowledgements
This issue was discovered by Maxime Escourbiac and Yassine Bengana (Michelin CERT).
The issue was fixed and coordinated by Steven Jin, Tabitha Sable, and Marco Ebert.

If you find evidence that this vulnerability has been exploited, please contact **security@kubernetes.io**

A security issue was discovered in [ingress-nginx](https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx) where the `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-method` Ingress annotation can be used to inject configuration into nginx. This can lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the ingress-nginx controller, and disclosure of Secrets accessible to the controller. (Note that in the default installation, the controller can access all Secrets cluster-wide.)

### Am I vulnerable?

This issue affects ingress-nginx. If you do not have ingress-nginx installed on your cluster, you are not affected. You can check this by running \`kubectl get pods \--all-namespaces \--selector app.kubernetes.io/name=ingress-nginx\`.

#### Affected Versions

- ingress-nginx: < v1.13.7
- ingress-nginx: < v1.14.3

### How do I mitigate this vulnerability?

ACTION REQUIRED: The following steps must be taken to mitigate this vulnerability: Upgrade ingress-nginx to v1.13.7, v1.14.3, or any later version.

Prior to upgrading, this vulnerability can be mitigated by using a validating admission controller to reject Ingress resources with the `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-method` annotation.

#### How to upgrade?

To upgrade, refer to the documentation: [Upgrading Ingress-nginx](https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx/deploy/upgrade/)

### Detection

Suspicious data within the `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-method` annotation of an Ingress resource could indicate an attempt to exploit this vulnerability.

### Acknowledgements
This issue was discovered by Volcengine Security Team.
The issue was fixed and coordinated by Steven Jin, Marco Ebert, and Tabitha Sable.

If you find evidence that this vulnerability has been exploited, please contact **security@kubernetes.io**

title: The externalTrafficPolicy configuration is invalid.
need_summary: Whether Kubernetes externalTrafficPolicy: Local on IPVS should reject cluster-external traffic sent to a node without local endpoints, and the answer rests on PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/97081 plus linked issues and maintainer comments explaining the behavior.
security_topic: external traffic handling for NodePort with externalTrafficPolicy Local on nodes without endpoints
question_text: Version 1.22 is too old. This PR (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/97081) was merged in 1.24 and was introduced to fix issues related to load balancers. It  change the behavior of external-net traffic arriving on a node without endpoints under ETP: Local  from being dropped directly to an indirect approach without SNAT.
answer_text:
Yes, I think you got it right. If a connect from a cluster-external source (that's what "external traffic" means), comes to a node without a local POD it is rejected, but in a "weird" way. This issue is about that it's *not* rejected, and I can only assume that it's CNI related.

Anyway, the external load-balancer should *not* route external traffic to a node without a serving POD, but that can of course happen occasionally on some reconfiguration event.

title: [failing-test] containerd serial tests failing on reboot
need_summary: Whether the kubelet crash on reboot is a security risk because ignoring the user-namespace length mismatch could let Kubelet re-allocate IDs and break pod isolation, as discussed in PR #136437 and PR #133373.
security_topic: Kubelet crash on user namespace length mismatch after reboot
question_text: Reaching out here before writing anything to gut check if this solution makes sense, as it's a bit more complex than just relaxing the check.
answer_text:
Hi @kannon92, I have already submitted a PR to address this exact Kubelet crash: #136437.

It modifies the UsernsManager to make these mismatching namespace lengths non-fatal, allowing Kubelet to start and log the error instead of crashing. I've addressed initial feedback from @chrishenzie. Ready for a quick look/review to get these jobs back to green!
thread_text:
ISSUE #136331: [failing-test] containerd serial tests failing on reboot
Author: kannon92
Date: 2026-01-20T01:39:36Z
Labels: priority/critical-urgent, sig/node, kind/failing-test, triage/accepted
State: closed

[c0]
### Which jobs are failing?

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-release-blocking#node-kubelet-serial-containerd

### Which tests are failing?

Right now the restart is causing all tests to fail.

It seems to only occur on cos as far as I could tell.

### Since when has it been failing?

At least for test grid its been failing like this for a few weeks now (Jan 04 2026)

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-release-blocking#node-kubelet-serial-containerd

### Reason for failure (if possible)

Its starting to look like the job is failing to restart kubelet causing the full test to fail.

https://storage.googleapis.com/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-serial-containerd/2013329922633764864/artifacts/e2-standard-2-cos-125-19216-104-95-334854fa/kubelet.log

```
E0119 19:53:13.251607  206171 run.go:72] "command failed" err="failed to run Kubelet: failed to create kubelet: create user namespace manager: record pod mappings for existing pod \"4cfeffa4-cc3a-4165-b92e-b48f481a0492\": wrong user namespace length 131072"
````

### Anything else we need to know?

Looks like Test started failing like this since January 14th. Before that we had failures related to credential provider. And then we are going complete failures since.

### Relevant SIG(s)

/sig node

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @kannon92 2026-01-20T01:40:30Z:
Marking this high priority because we are about to hit 1.36 with a serial jobs failing for containerd lanes.
---
[c2] @ShaanveerS 2026-01-21T20:34:13Z:
I found a timeline correlation dating back to the introduction of this logic. The same Prow failures appear as far back as Oct 24, 2025: https://storage.googleapis.com/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-serial-containerd/1981654007533277184/artifacts/e2-standard-2-cos-125-19216-0-100-d7076a4a/kubelet.log

This suggests the validation became unstable shortly after PR #133373 (Oct 18) which changed kubelet initialization so `userNamespaces.idsPerPod` is honored (previously it could be ignored) https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133373/changes#diff-d3d56ce70e5a8eff06a4274890a89b67ee72cc628a48ad84fb8033deff9123b5

If existing pods/checkpoints were created with 131072 but kubelet now comes up with 65536, kubelet fails when reconstructing mappings for existing pods after reboot, which matches the “restart causes everything to fail” pattern.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dff962ddbb0f5928086029e45a2fa63c28341c57/pkg/kubelet/kubeletconfig/defaults.go#L33

---
[c3] @chrishenzie 2026-01-21T22:55:44Z:
I tried mitigating this by logging the error instead of failing, but that seems unsafe. If `recordPodMappings` fails and we ignore it, the existing pod's ID range won't be marked in the bitmap, allowing Kubelet to re-allocate those IDs to other pods, which would break isolation as far as I understand.

I think the right fix might be to modify `record()` to handle length mismatches. It would need to calculate which bitmap slots are covered by the existing pod's range and mark them all as used. This ensures we don't crash on startup but also don't risk collisions.

Reaching out here before writing anything to gut check if this solution makes sense, as it's a bit more complex than just relaxing the check.
---
[c4] @kannon92 2026-01-24T12:44:52Z:
Looks like @dims found/fixed some of the bigger problems with this job.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136486
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136484

I'm not sure if the kubelet namespace errors are still a legit problem. But the test is now showing which tests actually fail.

@chrishenzie @MohammedSaalif

comments.author: ShaanveerS
comments.body:
I found a timeline correlation dating back to the introduction of this logic. The same Prow failures appear as far back as Oct 24, 2025: https://storage.googleapis.com/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet-serial-containerd/1981654007533277184/artifacts/e2-standard-2-cos-125-19216-0-100-d7076a4a/kubelet.log

This suggests the validation became unstable shortly after PR #133373 (Oct 18) which changed kubelet initialization so `userNamespaces.idsPerPod` is honored (previously it could be ignored) https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133373/changes#diff-d3d56ce70e5a8eff06a4274890a89b67ee72cc628a48ad84fb8033deff9123b5

If existing pods/checkpoints were created with 131072 but kubelet now comes up with 65536, kubelet fails when reconstructing mappings for existing pods after reboot, which matches the “restart causes everything to fail” pattern.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dff962ddbb0f5928086029e45a2fa63c28341c57/pkg/kubelet/kubeletconfig/defaults.go#L33

comments.author: chrishenzie
comments.body:
I tried mitigating this by logging the error instead of failing, but that seems unsafe. If `recordPodMappings` fails and we ignore it, the existing pod's ID range won't be marked in the bitmap, allowing Kubelet to re-allocate those IDs to other pods, which would break isolation as far as I understand.

I think the right fix might be to modify `record()` to handle length mismatches. It would need to calculate which bitmap slots are covered by the existing pod's range and mark them all as used. This ensures we don't crash on startup but also don't risk collisions.

Reaching out here before writing anything to gut check if this solution makes sense, as it's a bit more complex than just relaxing the check.

title: Unable to verify cosign signature for kubectl 1.35.0 on amd64
need_summary: Whether the kubectl release-signature verification failure was a Rekor transparency log validation issue and that it was resolved, as confirmed by the follow-up comment showing `Verified OK` and noting recent kpromo releases prevent this class of issue.
security_topic: cosign signature verification failure for a release artifact
question_text: After downloading kubectl 1.35.0, I attempted to verify the cosign keyless signature. This failed for amd64 but succeeds for arm64.
answer_text:
This issue no longer reproduces. Verification succeeds for both amd64 and arm64:

```bash
cosign verify-blob \
    --signature https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl.sig \
    --certificate https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl.cert \
    --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
    --certificate-identity krel-staging@k8s-releng-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
    https://dl.k8s.io/release/v1.35.0/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl
# Verified OK
```

The binary SHA256 matches the one reported in the issue (`a2e984a...0989`), so the artifact itself was never the problem. The original error (`invalid signature when validating ASN.1 encoded signature`) pointed to a Rekor transparency log validation issue that has since been resolved. Recent kpromo releases should also prevent this class of issue for future releases.

Closing as resolved. @nicholasdille feel free to reopen if you can still reproduce this.

question_text: When kubelet restarts, there is a race condition in `prober_manager.go` that causes pods that were NOT Ready before the restart to be briefly marked as Ready. This happens because:
answer_text:

thread_text:
ISSUE #135795: Kubelet restart causes NotReady pod to be briefly marked Ready before probe workers exist
Author: sanjams2
Date: 2025-12-17T14:26:02Z
Labels: sig/node, triage/needs-information
State: closed

[c0]
### What happened?

When kubelet restarts, there is a race condition in `prober_manager.go` that causes pods that were NOT Ready before the restart to be briefly marked as Ready. This happens because:

1. During `SyncPod`, `UpdatePodStatus` is called before prober workers are created
2. The code assumes "no worker exists = no readiness probe configured" and marks the container Ready
3. The pod is updated to Ready in the API server
4. Prober workers are then created and the first probe runs
5. The probe fails and the pod is marked NotReady again

This brief Ready window (we observed ~4 seconds) is enough for PodDisruptionBudget checks to succeed, allowing evictions that should have been blocked.

### Code Location

In `pkg/kubelet/prober/prober_manager.go`, the `UpdatePodStatus` function (around line 350):

```go
} else {
    // The check whether there is a probe which hasn't run yet.
    w, exists := m.getWorker(pod.UID, c.Name, readiness)
    ready = !exists // no readinessProbe -> always ready
```

The comment says "no readinessProbe -> always ready" but `exists` is false in TWO cases:
1. No readiness probe configured (intended)
2. Prober worker hasn't been created yet after kubelet restart (potential bug)

### Timeline from Production Incident

| Time (UTC) | Event | Source |
|------------|-------|--------|

1. During "First SyncPod Execution", the pod is marked Ready=true and API server is updated
2. The fix's precondition for "First Probe Execution" is "container Ready status is true"
3. But for pods that were NOT Ready before restart, the damage is already done - the API server was updated with Ready=true during SyncPod

Pods that were NOT Ready before kubelet restart should remain NOT Ready until probes pass. The kubelet should not assume "no worker = no probe configured" immediately after restart.

**Suggested Fix:**
During `UpdatePodStatus` after kubelet restart, if:
- No probe result exists in readinessManager
- No probe worker exists yet
- But the pod spec HAS a readiness probe configured

Then the container should be marked NOT Ready (or preserve the previous Ready state from API server) rather than assuming Ready.

### What happened?

When kubelet restarts, there is a race condition in `prober_manager.go` that causes pods that were NOT Ready before the restart to be briefly marked as Ready. This happens because:

1. During `SyncPod`, `UpdatePodStatus` is called before prober workers are created
2. The code assumes "no worker exists = no readiness probe configured" and marks the container Ready
3. The pod is updated to Ready in the API server
4. Prober workers are then created and the first probe runs
5. The probe fails and the pod is marked NotReady again

This brief Ready window (we observed ~4 seconds) is enough for PodDisruptionBudget checks to succeed, allowing evictions that should have been blocked.

### Code Location

In `pkg/kubelet/prober/prober_manager.go`, the `UpdatePodStatus` function (around line 350):

```go
} else {
    // The check whether there is a probe which hasn't run yet.
    w, exists := m.getWorker(pod.UID, c.Name, readiness)
    ready = !exists // no readinessProbe -> always ready
```

1. No readiness probe configured (intended)

title: DRA: Scheduler CEL evaluation fails with "no such key" when accessing nested attributes without existence check
need_summary: Whether CEL selectors for DRA should treat missing nested device attributes as false rather than a runtime error, and the answer is anchored in the Kubernetes API docs and CEL OptionalTypes documentation referenced by the maintainer.
security_topic: CEL selector behavior for missing nested attributes
question_text:
I am using DRA with a CEL selector to filter devices based on driver attributes. When writing an expression that accesses a nested field within `device.attributes`, the scheduler encounters a CEL runtime error if the specific driver key does not exist on the device, rather than evaluating the expression to false.

The following expression fails during the DynamicResources filter plugin execution:

```yaml
cel:
  expression: 'device.attributes["gpu.nvidia.com"].sharingStrategy == "runai-fractions"'
```
answer_text:
This works as designed and described:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/04d87a4b6e72336ee9afb1e5b477223c96a8fcbb/staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go#L1200-L1206

Tolerating this as you expected could have the effect that devices are not allocated as expected, so we wanted users to be aware that they have to be more precise in their selector.

What we can do is extend the documentation with an example:

    device.attributes["gpu.nvidia.com"].?sharingStrategy.orValue("") == "runai-fractions"'

This falls back to the empty string if `sharingStrategy` is not defined.
thread_text:
ISSUE #135661: DRA: Scheduler CEL evaluation fails with "no such key" when accessing nested attributes without existence check
Author: omeryahud
Date: 2025-12-08T11:25:59Z
Labels: kind/bug, needs-triage, wg/device-management
State: closed

[c0]
### What happened?

I am using DRA with a CEL selector to filter devices based on driver attributes. When writing an expression that accesses a nested field within `device.attributes`, the scheduler encounters a CEL runtime error if the specific driver key does not exist on the device, rather than evaluating the expression to false.

The following expression fails during the DynamicResources filter plugin execution:

```
cel:
  expression: 'device.attributes["gpu.nvidia.com"].sharingStrategy == "runai-fractions"'
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected the expression to evaluate to false for devices that do not possess the gpu.nvidia.com attribute, allowing the scheduler to simply skip those devices.

Instead, the scheduler treats this as a hard runtime error, preventing the claim from being allocated even if valid devices exist, or logging significant errors during the filter phase.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: DeviceClass
metadata:
  name: gpu.nvidia.com
spec:
  selectors:
  - cel: 
      expression: "device.driver == 'gpu.nvidia.com'"
---
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: ResourceSlice
metadata:
  name: kind-control-plane-gpu-devices-slice
spec:
  nodeName: kind-control-plane
  driver: gpu.nvidia.com

  pool:
    generation: 1
    resourceSliceCount: 1
    name: kind-control-plane-gpu-pool

  devices:
  - name: gpu-0
    bindsToNode: true

  - name: gpu-1
    attributes:
      sharingStrategy:
        string: runai-fractions
    bindsToNode: true
---
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: ResourceClaim
metadata:
  name: kind-control-plane-gpu-runai-fractionable-claim-1
spec:
  devices:
    requests:
    - name: gpu-runai-fractionable
      exactly:
        deviceClassName: gpu.nvidia.com
        capacity:
          requests:
            memory: 10Gi
        selectors:
        - cel:
            expression: 'device.attributes["gpu.nvidia.com"].sharingStrategy == "runai-fractions"'
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: fraction-pod-1
spec:
  resourceClaims:
  - name: fraction-claim
    resourceClaimName: kind-control-plane-gpu-runai-fractionable-claim-1
  containers:
  - name: fraction-container
    resources:
      claims:
      - name: fraction-claim
    image: ubuntu:latest
    command: [ "/bin/bash", "-c", "--" ]
    args: [sleep Infinity"]
```

```
> kubectl describe pod fraction-pod-1
...
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age              From               Message
  ----     ------            ----             ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  3s               default-scheduler  0/1 nodes are available: 1 cannot allocate all claims. still not schedulable, preemption: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.
  Warning  FailedScheduling  1s (x2 over 3s)  default-scheduler  running "DynamicResources" filter plugin: claim default/kind-control-plane-gpu-runai-fractionable-claim-1: selector #0: CEL runtime error: no such key: sharingStrategy
```


### Anything else we need to know?

With PartitionableDevices and ConsumableCapacity feature gates enabled

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version  
Client Version: v1.34.2
Kustomize Version: v5.7.1
Server Version: v1.34.0
```

</details>
