ISSUE #133897: CVE-2025-7445: secrets-store-sync-controller discloses service account tokens in logs
Author: enj
Date: 2025-09-04T21:40:42Z
Labels: kind/bug, area/security, sig/auth, committee/security-response, triage/accepted, official-cve-feed
State: closed

[c0]
A security issue was discovered in [secrets-store-sync-controller](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/secrets-store-sync-controller) where an actor with access to the controller logs could observe service account tokens.  These tokens could then potentially be exchanged with external cloud providers to access secrets stored in cloud vault solutions.  Tokens are only logged when there is a specific error marshaling the `parameters` sent to the providers.

This issue has been rated MEDIUM [CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N) (6.5), and assigned CVE-2025-7445

### Am I vulnerable?

To check if tokens are being logged, examine the manager container log:

```bash
kubectl logs -l 'app.kubernetes.io/part-of=secrets-store-sync-controller' -c manager -f | grep --line-buffered "csi.storage.k8s.io/serviceAccount.tokens"
```

### Affected Versions

- secrets-store-sync-controller < v0.0.2

### How do I mitigate this vulnerability?

Upgrade to secrets-store-sync-controller v0.0.2+

### Fixed Versions

- secrets-store-sync-controller >= v0.0.2


### Detection

Examine cloud provider logs for unexpected token exchanges, as well as unexpected access to cloud vault secrets.

If you find evidence that this vulnerability has been exploited, please contact [security@kubernetes.io](https://groups.google.com/)

### Acknowledgements

This vulnerability was reported by Reem Rotenberg and [Kas Dekel](https://github.com/privmickas) from Microsoft.

title: [Flaking Test] integration TestConcurrencyIsolation
need_summary: Whether the flaky TestConcurrencyIsolation failure was just a noisy performance-tolerance problem in the test, and the answer is anchored on PR #135464 plus the maintainer’s explanation of the corrected error-margin formula.
security_topic: test flake due to concurrency/performance-tolerance calculation
question_text:
@pohly https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133781(merged 12 hours ago) is this related? 

I did a quick go through recent merged PRs and only this is related to priority classes. But I still don't know if it is related or not.
answer_text:
The comment at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/133861#issuecomment-3858531389 elides almost all of each relevant log message! Impossible to understand.

I looked at the two latest failures from testgrid, https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-integration-master/2019516018384179200 and https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-integration-master/2019242966542979072

This test is NOT verifying absolute performance. It is comparing the service delivered to two concurrent request streams that should get different results, and testing whether the results differ as expected. With tolerance for deviation from the ideal result. That tolerance is calculated by a formula. Following are the relevant lines from those two runs.

> concurrency_util_test.go:286: Error margin is 0.007326905866825164
> concurrency_util_test.go:290: noxu1 relative error is 0.009741628939946321

> concurrency_util_test.go:286: Error margin is 0.00812468852781139
> concurrency_util_test.go:290: noxu1 relative error is 0.010958869921903987

These show that the results differed by a little more than the formula expected. I have since come to the opinion that the formula being used is wrong (because it takes into account the noise experienced by only one of the two request streams), and made a PR that changes the formula to something better (i.e., take into account the noise experienced by both request streams). That is #135464 . Its formula for the acceptable relative error would not fail the above cases.

This test is NOT verifying absolute performance. It is comparing the service delivered to two concurrent request streams that should get different results, and testing whether the results differ as expected. With tolerance for deviation from the ideal result. That tolerance is calculated by a formula. Following are the relevant lines from those two runs.

> concurrency_util_test.go:286: Error margin is 0.007326905866825164
> concurrency_util_test.go:290: noxu1 relative error is 0.009741628939946321

> concurrency_util_test.go:290: noxu1 relative error is 0.010958869921903987

These show that the results differed by a little more than the formula expected. I have since come to the opinion that the formula being used is wrong (because it takes into account the noise experienced by only one of the two request streams), and made a PR that changes the formula to something better (i.e., take into account the noise experienced by both request streams). That is #135464 . Its formula for the acceptable relative error would not fail the above cases.

ISSUE #133689: [node] Missing conformance endpoints for podexec / portforward using POST (and namespaced) (2 operations)
Author: dims

[c0]
https://apisnoop.cncf.io/conformance-progress/endpoints/1.34.0/?filter=untested

we are missing the following:
- connectCoreV1PostNamespacedPodExec
- connectCoreV1PostNamespacedPodPortforward


/sig node
/sig architecture
/area conformance

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @pohly 2025-08-25T14:45:38Z:
Why are those not covered? Aren't those old endpoints which should have been covered already when 100% coverage was achieved?

[c2] @dims 2025-08-28T13:57:55Z:

[c3] @liggitt 2025-08-28T15:22:00Z:
> @pohly github search does not reveal the mystery to me yet..

The POST vs GET distinction for pods/exec, pods/attach, and pods/portforward is the difference between using spdy and using websockets.

kubectl 1.31+ switched from using spdy (via POST) to websockets (via GET), because upgraded spdy POST requests to the server don't work reliably through some proxies. See:

* https://kubernetes.io/blog/2024/08/20/websockets-transition/
* https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/4006-transition-spdy-to-websockets

I think `kubectl exec` *happened* to be used as part of various tests which *happened* to be conformance tests, and that was the only thing exercising SPDY POST requests. When `kubectl exec` switched to websockets, that left SPDY POST requests for those handlers unexercised in conformance tests. 

With kubectl switching to use websocket GET as well, and SPDY POST being unreliable / deprecated (so unreliable it justified that KEP and the work to switch kubectl), I actually think it's fine to mark the SPDY POST pods/exec endpoint as ineligible for conformance (it is likely some clusters using some proxies *couldn't* pass conformance if supporting SPDY POST was required).

We have long had a conformance test explicitly exercising websocket pods/exec via GET, so excluding connectCoreV1PostNamespacedPodExec because pods/exec is a debug endpoint doesn't make much sense:
```
framework.ConformanceIt("should support remote command execution over websockets", f.WithNodeConformance(), func(ctx context.Context) {
```

Excluding connectCoreV1PostNamespacedPodExec because that is a deprecated and sometimes-unreliable SPDY protocol would make more sense to me.

Separately, we should consider whether we want to treat pods/attach and pods/portforward consistently with pods/exec (exercise and require the websocket GET versions in conformance, mark the spdy POST versions ineligible for conformance). It sort of seems like we should.
---
[c4] @BenTheElder 2025-08-28T18:21:27Z:
+1

> Excluding connectCoreV1PostNamespacedPodExec because that is a deprecated and sometimes-unreliable SPDY protocol would make more sense to me.

Not strictly related, but do we have a documented timeline for deprecating these generally?

Still makes sense to soft-deprecate by dropping from conformance, given the reliability issues.
---
[c5] @liggitt 2025-08-28T18:24:45Z:
> Not strictly related, but do we have a documented timeline for deprecating these generally?

No, since they're v1, I'd expect we'd mark as deprecated but not remove them. There's not much benefit to switching for folks for whom the spdy version is working in their environment.
---
[c6] @BenTheElder 2025-08-28T18:35:41Z:
> No, since they're v1, I'd expect we'd mark as deprecated but not remove them. There's not much benefit to switching for folks for whom the spdy version is working in their environment.

Eventually this seems like an unmaintained dependency risk? Is there a more appropriate thread for this topic?

I guess github.com/moby/spdystream is pretty small without external deps.
---
[c7] @liggitt 2025-08-28T18:38:22Z:
We're still using SPDY from apiserver -> kubelet, sadly, so ... we'll still actively exercising it, and it's contained / zero-dep... it's not in the top of half of dependencies I'm concerned about
---
[c8] @dims 2025-09-01T23:17:23Z:
Added it to ineligible_endpoints.yaml:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/conformance/testdata/ineligible_endpoints.yaml#L298-L303

title: DRA extended resources resourcequota
need_summary: Whether the DRA extended resource quota counting issue was resolved by PR #134210, which adjusted quota accounting at resource claim admission time.
security_topic: resource quota accounting across DRA and extended resources
question_text: With the approach described in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/133671#issuecomment-3246085820, what quota(s) should be defined to limit the number of mygpu devices in a namespace (e.g. to 10) across all of those consumption patterns?
answer_text:
[DRA extended resource quota #134210](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134210) implements the adjustment of resource quota  at the resource claim admission time for quotaC and quotaD below.

before adjustment:
quotaC: request.example.com/gpu = case1 + case2
quotaD: request.deviceclass.resource.kubernetes.io/mygpuclass = case3

after adjustment:
quotaC: request.example.com/gpu = case1 + case2 + case3 + case4 + case5
quotaD: request.deviceclass.resource.kubernetes.io/mygpuclass = case3 + case2 + case4 + case5

quotaA remains unchanged, as it correctly counts all the devices usages from resource claims
quotaB  is not added as originally planned for the controller based quota adjustment. It is no longer needed for this admission time quota adjustment.

the main logic is inside resource claims quota evaluator. Please take a look. @liggitt

ISSUE #133671: DRA extended resources resourcequota
Author: yliaog
Date: 2025-08-23T21:08:25Z
Labels: needs-triage, wg/device-management
State: closed

[c0]
[KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-scheduling/5004-dra-extended-resource#resource-quota) discussed the resource quota for DRA extended resources. It needs to be discussed, and implemented for DRA extended resources Beta.

--- COMMENTS ---

[c2] @bitoku 2025-08-28T17:09:50Z:
What we want to do is:
 - both `extended resource name` and `implicit extended resource name` are configurable in resource quota.
 - Whichever lower is regarded as the actual quota and shares the quota bucket.
 - Even if it uses DRA directly or DRA extended resource, resource claim is used as a source of usage count.

Right? Correct me if I'm wrong.
---
[c3] @yliaog 2025-08-28T18:08:13Z:
> What we want to do is:
> 
> * both `extended resource name` and `implicit extended resource name` are configurable in resource quota.
> * Whichever lower is regarded as the actual quota and shares the quota bucket.
> * Even if it uses DRA directly or DRA extended resource, resource claim is used as a source of usage count.
>

usage can come for either DRA extended resource, or from resource claim.

when user provides quota for both, the system should take the lower limit as the real limit for both

when user provides quota for only one, the system should use that limit, and still tracks usage from both sources

---
[c4] @bitoku 2025-08-28T18:17:11Z:
> usage can come for either DRA extended resource, or from resource claim.

But with DRA extended resource, the resource claim is automatically created, isn't it?
Isn't it easier to use only resource claim than using both?

---
[c5] @yliaog 2025-08-28T18:26:46Z:
extended resource can provide usage for both device plugin, and DRA devices. if there were no former, only the latter, then extended resource is equivalent to resource claim, it is just another way of creating resource claim (automatically by scheduler).
---
[c6] @bitoku 2025-08-29T10:31:10Z:
Thank you for clarification. I didn't understand how resource quota works.
So extended resource usage is managed by [podEvaluator](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/eb0f003d25209c850b47a275358aea53252274b4/pkg/quota/v1/evaluator/core/pods.go#L109-L115) and resource claim usage is managed by [claimEvaluator](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c4f81743c2ee73fae71d336304e491b2539b6e3/pkg/quota/v1/evaluator/core/resource_claims.go#L52-L56).
We need something to share the extended resource quota and resource claim quota for DRA extended resource.
The complicated part is that resource claim can be created without extended resource.

---
[c7] @bitoku 2025-08-29T10:34:12Z:
Also thanks for the offline discussion about [DRA resource quota](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/4381-dra-structured-parameters#resourcequota).
Based on it, these three resource quota should be treated as the same quota. They all refers to the same device class.

- `<device-class-name>.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/devices`
- `deviceclass.resource.kubernetes.io/<device-class-name>`
- `<extended-resource-name>`
---
[c8] @yliaog 2025-08-29T18:17:51Z:
there are two ways (we can leave out the implicit extended resource name for this discussion, as it can be dealt with in the same way as explicit extended resource name) to quota the same class of devices

1. <device-class-name>.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/devices: quota devices provided from DRA resource slices
1. extended resource quota: quota the devices provided from the sum of device plugin + DRA resource slice (when DRAExtendedResources feature is enabled)

cluster admin can decide to quota only the DRA devices, in that case, they can use just the first quota mechanism, or a cluster amdin can decide to quota only the sum of DRA + Device Plugin devices, and in that case, they can use just the second quota mechanism. or a cluster admin may decide to quota both the DRA devices and the sum of DRA + Device Plugin devices, for that, they can specify both the first and second quota mechanism, and in the case, the quota limit for the second quota mechanism *MUST* be greater than or equal to the limit of the first quota mechanism.

when a cluster admin only uses the first quota mechanism, the usage is properly counted no matter it is coming from the resource claim, or from the extended resource requests, this is due to the fact that scheduler automatically creates a resource claim for that extended resource requests.

the problem arises when a cluster admin uses the second quota mechanism, at the moment, the usage coming from resource claim is *NOT* counted in the extended resource quota. This is what needs to be resolved, i.e., properly count the usage from resource claim in the extended resource quota.
---
[c9] @yliaog 2025-08-29T18:39:27Z:
what is proposed in the KEP is to reconcile the counting of the usage from resource claim with the extended resource quota in the resource quota controller. The alternative is to reconcile the counting at the resource claim admission time. Reconcile the counting at the resource quota controller is easier to implement, but less precise (as the controller only does this reconcilation periodically).
---
[c10] @yliaog 2025-09-02T16:48:32Z:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133789 implemented the reconcilation at the quota controller. In addtiion to the two quotas: one for the total resource claims, one for the extended resources, the PR added another quota: for the regular resource claims (i.e. excluding those claims created by the scheduler for the extended resources). hence there are three quotas (2/ is newly added).

1/ # of devices for a deviceclass for all resource claims (regular claim + extended resource claim)
**_2/ # of devices for a deviceclass for regular claims_**
3/ # of devices for an extended resource (matching the device class) == # of devices provided by device plugin + # of devices provided by extended resource claim 

we need to adjust 3/ such that the usage from regular claims are counted in the extended resource quota usage. 
3/ # of devices for an extended resource (matching the device class) == # of devices provided by device plugin + # of devices provided by extended resource claim + **_# of devices for a deviceclass for regular claims_**

---
[c11] @yliaog 2025-09-02T16:50:50Z:
@liggitt could you take a look at the comment above, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/133671#issuecomment-3246085820 ?
---
[c12] @bitoku 2025-09-04T17:11:42Z:
@yliaog This sounds like a good approach to me.
BTW, we need to care about multiple device classes for one extended resource due to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/133693 , but we just count all related device classes, right? not only one picked up.
---
[c13] @liggitt 2025-09-04T21:27:14Z:
> [@liggitt](https://github.com/liggitt) could you take a look at the comment above, [#133671 (comment)](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/133671#issuecomment-3246085820) ?

I'm having a little bit of a hard time following https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/133671#issuecomment-3246085820 and visualizing all the ways a device could be addressed, and what quota(s) should be set to make sure use across DRA and legacy deviceplugins is bounded without double-counting ... maybe an example would help?

Setup:
* extended resource `example.com/mygpu`
* deviceclass `mygpuclass` with `extendedResourceName: example.com/mygpu`

Those devices can be consumed via:
1. pods requesting `resources: {example.com/mygpu: 2}` resulting in direct use on legacy deviceplugin nodes
2. pods requesting `resources: {example.com/mygpu: 2}` resulting in a scheduler-created ResourceClaim on new DRA nodes
3. pods requesting `resources: {deviceclass.resource.kubernetes.io/mygpuclass: 2}` resulting in a scheduler-created ResourceClaim on new DRA nodes
4. pods referencing a user-created ResourceClaim with `deviceClassName: mygpuclass`
5. pods with a resourceClaimTemplateName pointing at a ResourceClaimTemplate with `deviceClassName: mygpuclass` (results in a controller-created ResourceClaim)

With the approach described in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/133671#issuecomment-3246085820, what quota(s) should be defined to limit the number of mygpu devices in a namespace (e.g. to 10) across all of those consumption patterns?
---
[c14] @yliaog 2025-09-04T21:50:04Z:
1/ mygpuclass.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/devices: 10 this is the currently existing DRA resource claim quota, it would quota examples 2. 3. 4. 5 above.
2/ mygpuclass.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/non-extended-resource-devices: 10: this is the proposed new quota, to be added, it is for regular DRA resource claim only, i.e., it excludes the special extended resource claim. it would quota the examples 4. and 5. above.
3/ requests.example.com/gpu: 10: this is the existing extended resource quota, it could be allocated from device plugin devices or DRA devices. it currently would only quota the examples 1. 2. 3. given above. with the proposed proof of concept PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133789, it would quota all of the 5 example cases above.
---
[c15] @liggitt 2025-09-04T22:05:05Z:
> 1/ mygpuclass.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/devices: 10 this is the currently existing DRA resource claim quota, it would quota examples 2. 3. 4. 5 above.

That seems great for things which have no legacy extended resource addressability. Does case 2 and 3 get blocked at pod create time or at resourceclaim create time?

> 2/ mygpuclass.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/non-extended-resource-devices: 10: this is the proposed new quota, to be added, it is for regular DRA resource claim only, i.e., it excludes the special extended resource claim. it would quota the examples 4. and 5. above.

Why do we need to address this separately? It seems like `requests.example.com/mygpu` is simpler

> 3/ requests.example.com/gpu: 10: this is the existing extended resource quota, it could be allocated from device plugin devices or DRA devices. it currently would only quota the examples 1. 2. 3. given above. with the proposed proof of concept PR [#133789](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133789), it would quota all of the 5 example cases above.

This seems great if we can accomplish it. Does that involve these changes to quota admission and controller?

A) (to cover example 3) count a pod request for `deviceclass.resource.kubernetes.io/mygpuclass` as also being a request for the same quantity for that device class's `extendedResourceName: example.com/mygpu`?

B) (to cover example 4,5 without double-counting 2) only count non-scheduler created resourceclaim with `deviceClassName: mygpuclass` as also being a request for that device class's `extendedResourceName: example.com/mygpu`? How is that done in a way that can't be spoofed?
---
[c16] @yliaog 2025-09-05T16:22:40Z:
case 2 and 3 get blocked at at resourceclaim create time

this proposal, and POC PR does the usage reconcilation / adjustment at the quota controller, not at the pod or claim admission time. so there might be a lag, that causes pod or claim to be admitted while over the quota. when the next quota controller reconcile loop runs, the usage will be corrected. and after that, no more pod or claim can be admitted if already over quota.

Now the details, there are actaully four related quotas, when calling quota.CalculateUsage(resourceQuota.Namespace, resourceQuota.Spec.Scopes, hardLimits, rq.registry, resourceQuota.Spec.ScopeSelector), the usage for the four quotas are:

quotaA: mygpuclass.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/devices = case2 + case3 + case4 + case5
quotaB: mygpuclass.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/non-extended-resource-devices = case4 + case5
quotaC: request.example.com/gpu = case1 + case2
quotaD: request.deviceclass.resource.kubernetes.io/mygpuclass = case3

Now we have the real usage for the four quotas,

if user creates resource quota object with request.example.com/gpu, we want to adjust their usage in the resource quota controller to count in the usage from other cases, the total count of usage would be adjusted from case1 + case2 to case1+case2+case3+case4+case5 = quotaB + quotaC + quotaD

if user creates resource quota object with request.deviceclass.resource.kubernetes.io/mygpuclass, we want to adjust their usage in the resource quota controller to count in the usage from ohter cases, the total count of usage would be adjusted from case3 to case2 + case3 + case4 + case5 = quotaA
---
[c17] @liggitt 2025-09-16T16:39:59Z:
> this proposal, and POC PR does the usage reconcilation / adjustment at the quota controller, not at the pod or claim admission time

oh... I missed that ... shouldn't we be able to recognize the consumed usage either at pod admission time or at claim admission time using the same logic the controller would use asynchronously? why do we have to skip enforcement at admission time?
---
[c18] @yliaog 2025-09-16T18:26:31Z:
> > this proposal, and POC PR does the usage reconcilation / adjustment at the quota controller, not at the pod or claim admission time
> 
> oh... I missed that ... shouldn't we be able to recognize the consumed usage either at pod admission time or at claim admission time using the same logic the controller would use asynchronously? why do we have to skip enforcement at admission time?

the major reason is the performance (latency), we can call quota.CalculateUsage(resourceQuota.Namespace, resourceQuota.Spec.Scopes, hardLimits, rq.registry, resourceQuota.Spec.ScopeSelector) in controller asynchronously, but i'm afraid it is too expensive to call it at the pod admission time.
---
[c19] @liggitt 2025-09-17T19:55:49Z:
> the major reason is the performance (latency), we can call quota.CalculateUsage(resourceQuota.Namespace, resourceQuota.Spec.Scopes, hardLimits, rq.registry, resourceQuota.Spec.ScopeSelector) in controller asynchronously, but i'm afraid it is too expensive to call it at the pod admission time.

I can see that for fully recalculating, but can we not determine how much the pod or claim being created or updated should count against the extended resource at admission time? It seems pretty bad to not enforce at all in admission and count on reconciliation to later lock stuff down
---
[c20] @yliaog 2025-09-17T23:11:48Z:
> I can see that for fully recalculating, but can we not determine how much the pod or claim being created or updated should count against the extended resource at admission time? It seems pretty bad to not enforce at all in admission and count on reconciliation to later lock stuff down

we cannot do the admission time usage adjustment unless we require users to  always set the resourceclaim quota when they set the extended resource quota. If a user sets only the extended resource quota request.example.com/gpu: 10, then at the resourceclaim admission time, the resourceclaim quota evaluator won't be called, then there is no way to add the usage from the resource claim to that extended resource quota usage.

On the other hand, if user always sets the four quotas, then at the resource claim admission time, we can simply adjust the corresponding extended resource quota's usage in its resource claim's quota evaluator, based on the same adjustment as the controller takes.

quotaA: mygpuclass.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/devices = case2 + case3 + case4 + case5
quotaB: mygpuclass.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/non-extended-resource-devices = case4 + case5
quotaC: request.example.com/gpu = case1 + case2

comments.author: bitoku

comments.author: bitoku
comments.body:
Also thanks for the offline discussion about [DRA resource quota](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/4381-dra-structured-parameters#resourcequota).
Based on it, these three resource quota should be treated as the same quota. They all refers to the same device class.

- `<device-class-name>.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/devices`
- `deviceclass.resource.kubernetes.io/<device-class-name>`
- `<extended-resource-name>`

comments.author: yliaog
comments.body:
there are two ways (we can leave out the implicit extended resource name for this discussion, as it can be dealt with in the same way as explicit extended resource name) to quota the same class of devices

1. <device-class-name>.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/devices: quota devices provided from DRA resource slices
1. extended resource quota: quota the devices provided from the sum of device plugin + DRA resource slice (when DRAExtendedResources feature is enabled)

cluster admin can decide to quota only the DRA devices, in that case, they can use just the first quota mechanism, or a cluster amdin can decide to quota only the sum of DRA + Device Plugin devices, and in that case, they can use just the second quota mechanism. or a cluster admin may decide to quota both the DRA devices and the sum of DRA + Device Plugin devices, for that, they can specify both the first and second quota mechanism, and in the case, the quota limit for the second quota mechanism *MUST* be greater than or equal to the limit of the first quota mechanism.

when a cluster admin only uses the first quota mechanism, the usage is properly counted no matter it is coming from the resource claim, or from the extended resource requests, this is due to the fact that scheduler automatically creates a resource claim for that extended resource requests.

the problem arises when a cluster admin uses the second quota mechanism, at the moment, the usage coming from resource claim is *NOT* counted in the extended resource quota. This is what needs to be resolved, i.e., properly count the usage from resource claim in the extended resource quota.

comments.author: yliaog
comments.body: what is proposed in the KEP is to reconcile the counting of the usage from resource claim with the extended resource quota in the resource quota controller. The alternative is to reconcile the counting at the resource claim admission time. Reconcile the counting at the resource quota controller is easier to implement, but less precise (as the controller only does this reconcilation periodically).

comments.author: yliaog
comments.body:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133789 implemented the reconcilation at the quota controller. In addtiion to the two quotas: one for the total resource claims, one for the extended resources, the PR added another quota: for the regular resource claims (i.e. excluding those claims created by the scheduler for the extended resources). hence there are three quotas (2/ is newly added).

1/ # of devices for a deviceclass for all resource claims (regular claim + extended resource claim)
**_2/ # of devices for a deviceclass for regular claims_**
3/ # of devices for an extended resource (matching the device class) == # of devices provided by device plugin + # of devices provided by extended resource claim 

we need to adjust 3/ such that the usage from regular claims are counted in the extended resource quota usage. 
3/ # of devices for an extended resource (matching the device class) == # of devices provided by device plugin + # of devices provided by extended resource claim + **_# of devices for a deviceclass for regular claims_**

comments.author: liggitt
comments.body:
> [@liggitt](https://github.com/liggitt) could you take a look at the comment above, [#133671 (comment)](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/133671#issuecomment-3246085820) ?

I'm having a little bit of a hard time following https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/133671#issuecomment-3246085820 and visualizing all the ways a device could be addressed, and what quota(s) should be set to make sure use across DRA and legacy deviceplugins is bounded without double-counting ... maybe an example would help?

Setup:
* extended resource `example.com/mygpu`
* deviceclass `mygpuclass` with `extendedResourceName: example.com/mygpu`

Those devices can be consumed via:
1. pods requesting `resources: {example.com/mygpu: 2}` resulting in direct use on legacy deviceplugin nodes
2. pods requesting `resources: {example.com/mygpu: 2}` resulting in a scheduler-created ResourceClaim on new DRA nodes
3. pods requesting `resources: {deviceclass.resource.kubernetes.io/mygpuclass: 2}` resulting in a scheduler-created ResourceClaim on new DRA nodes
4. pods referencing a user-created ResourceClaim with `deviceClassName: mygpuclass`
5. pods with a resourceClaimTemplateName pointing at a ResourceClaimTemplate with `deviceClassName: mygpuclass` (results in a controller-created ResourceClaim)

With the approach described in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/133671#issuecomment-3246085820, what quota(s) should be defined to limit the number of mygpu devices in a namespace (e.g. to 10) across all of those consumption patterns?

comments.author: yliaog
comments.body:
1/ mygpuclass.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/devices: 10 this is the currently existing DRA resource claim quota, it would quota examples 2. 3. 4. 5 above.
2/ mygpuclass.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/non-extended-resource-devices: 10: this is the proposed new quota, to be added, it is for regular DRA resource claim only, i.e., it excludes the special extended resource claim. it would quota the examples 4. and 5. above.
3/ requests.example.com/gpu: 10: this is the existing extended resource quota, it could be allocated from device plugin devices or DRA devices. it currently would only quota the examples 1. 2. 3. given above. with the proposed proof of concept PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133789, it would quota all of the 5 example cases above.

comments.body:
> 1/ mygpuclass.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/devices: 10 this is the currently existing DRA resource claim quota, it would quota examples 2. 3. 4. 5 above.

> 2/ mygpuclass.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/non-extended-resource-devices: 10: this is the proposed new quota, to be added, it is for regular DRA resource claim only, i.e., it excludes the special extended resource claim. it would quota the examples 4. and 5. above.

Why do we need to address this separately? It seems like `requests.example.com/mygpu` is simpler

This seems great if we can accomplish it. Does that involve these changes to quota admission and controller?

A) (to cover example 3) count a pod request for `deviceclass.resource.kubernetes.io/mygpuclass` as also being a request for the same quantity for that device class's `extendedResourceName: example.com/mygpu`?

B) (to cover example 4,5 without double-counting 2) only count non-scheduler created resourceclaim with `deviceClassName: mygpuclass` as also being a request for that device class's `extendedResourceName: example.com/mygpu`? How is that done in a way that can't be spoofed?

comments.author: yliaog
comments.body:
case 2 and 3 get blocked at at resourceclaim create time

this proposal, and POC PR does the usage reconcilation / adjustment at the quota controller, not at the pod or claim admission time. so there might be a lag, that causes pod or claim to be admitted while over the quota. when the next quota controller reconcile loop runs, the usage will be corrected. and after that, no more pod or claim can be admitted if already over quota.

Now the details, there are actaully four related quotas, when calling quota.CalculateUsage(resourceQuota.Namespace, resourceQuota.Spec.Scopes, hardLimits, rq.registry, resourceQuota.Spec.ScopeSelector), the usage for the four quotas are:

quotaA: mygpuclass.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/devices = case2 + case3 + case4 + case5
quotaB: mygpuclass.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/non-extended-resource-devices = case4 + case5
quotaC: request.example.com/gpu = case1 + case2
quotaD: request.deviceclass.resource.kubernetes.io/mygpuclass = case3

Now we have the real usage for the four quotas,

if user creates resource quota object with request.example.com/gpu, we want to adjust their usage in the resource quota controller to count in the usage from other cases, the total count of usage would be adjusted from case1 + case2 to case1+case2+case3+case4+case5 = quotaB + quotaC + quotaD

if user creates resource quota object with request.deviceclass.resource.kubernetes.io/mygpuclass, we want to adjust their usage in the resource quota controller to count in the usage from ohter cases, the total count of usage would be adjusted from case3 to case2 + case3 + case4 + case5 = quotaA

> this proposal, and POC PR does the usage reconcilation / adjustment at the quota controller, not at the pod or claim admission time

oh... I missed that ... shouldn't we be able to recognize the consumed usage either at pod admission time or at claim admission time using the same logic the controller would use asynchronously? why do we have to skip enforcement at admission time?

comments.author: yliaog
comments.body:
> > this proposal, and POC PR does the usage reconcilation / adjustment at the quota controller, not at the pod or claim admission time
> 
> oh... I missed that ... shouldn't we be able to recognize the consumed usage either at pod admission time or at claim admission time using the same logic the controller would use asynchronously? why do we have to skip enforcement at admission time?

the major reason is the performance (latency), we can call quota.CalculateUsage(resourceQuota.Namespace, resourceQuota.Spec.Scopes, hardLimits, rq.registry, resourceQuota.Spec.ScopeSelector) in controller asynchronously, but i'm afraid it is too expensive to call it at the pod admission time.

comments.author: liggitt
comments.body:
> the major reason is the performance (latency), we can call quota.CalculateUsage(resourceQuota.Namespace, resourceQuota.Spec.Scopes, hardLimits, rq.registry, resourceQuota.Spec.ScopeSelector) in controller asynchronously, but i'm afraid it is too expensive to call it at the pod admission time.

I can see that for fully recalculating, but can we not determine how much the pod or claim being created or updated should count against the extended resource at admission time? It seems pretty bad to not enforce at all in admission and count on reconciliation to later lock stuff down

comments.author: yliaog
comments.body:
> I can see that for fully recalculating, but can we not determine how much the pod or claim being created or updated should count against the extended resource at admission time? It seems pretty bad to not enforce at all in admission and count on reconciliation to later lock stuff down

we cannot do the admission time usage adjustment unless we require users to  always set the resourceclaim quota when they set the extended resource quota. If a user sets only the extended resource quota request.example.com/gpu: 10, then at the resourceclaim admission time, the resourceclaim quota evaluator won't be called, then there is no way to add the usage from the resource claim to that extended resource quota usage.

On the other hand, if user always sets the four quotas, then at the resource claim admission time, we can simply adjust the corresponding extended resource quota's usage in its resource claim's quota evaluator, based on the same adjustment as the controller takes.

quotaA: mygpuclass.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/devices = case2 + case3 + case4 + case5
quotaB: mygpuclass.deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/non-extended-resource-devices = case4 + case5
quotaC: request.example.com/gpu = case1 + case2
quotaD: request.deviceclass.resource.kubernetes.io/mygpuclass = case3

We get to define which resource types evaluators get called on, and our evaluator can use an informer in the background to tell that a device class is associated with extended resources and account for them while admitting resource claims for those device classes, right?

comments.body:
[DRA extended resource quota #134210](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134210) implements the adjustment of resource quota  at the resource claim admission time for quotaC and quotaD below.

before adjustment:
quotaC: request.example.com/gpu = case1 + case2

after adjustment:

title: Debian now deprecates public key file used for K8s APT repo
need_summary: Whether the Debian APT repository key warning is a security issue and should be tracked under the linked kubernetes/release issue #3869 as the concrete source.
security_topic: APT repository key signature/hash algorithm deprecation
question_text:
Hi, the K8s repo at https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/v1.33/deb/ uses a public key file having a hashing algorithm which Debian APT no longer considers safe.  The message emitted by APT (in response to command `apt update`) is:
```
Warning: https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/v1.33/deb/InRelease: Policy will reject signature within a year, see --audit for details
```
The command `apt update --audit` outputs:
```
Warning: https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/v1.33/deb/InRelease: Policy will reject signature within a year, see --audit for details
Audit: https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/v1.33/deb/InRelease: Sub-process /usr/bin/sqv returned an error code (1), error message is:
   Error: Policy rejected packet type
   Caused by:
       Signature Packet v3 is not considered secure since 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z
```
As I understand it, this would be because the public key is hashed using SHA1, rather than SHA256 or SHA512.  

I can suppress this warning (presumably until 1 February 2026) by copying file `/usr/share/apt/default-sequoia.config` to new file (in new parent directories) `/etc/crypto-policies/back-ends/apt-sequoia.config`, and changing the date in the last line from `2026-02-01` to `2027-02-01`.
answer_text:
This is already being tracked as part of https://github.com/kubernetes/release/issues/3869
>/close

title: Request method of  `kubectl exec` changed from `POST` to `GET` now?
need_summary: Whether kubectl exec’s switch from POST/create to GET/get weakened the RBAC boundary, and the answer is anchored by the maintainer comments citing the websockets GET behavior plus PR #134577 and Kubernetes enhancement PR #5524 for restoring the create check in 1.35.0+.
security_topic: RBAC permission change for kubectl exec transport
question_text:
Why has the request method of  `kubectl exec`  changed from `POST` to `GET` now, eg, v1.33.3. It was `POST` in `v1.26.15`?
And now `pods/exec` no need `create` verbs, `get` is enough to make it happen, is it intended?
answer_text:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134577 synthetically added checks for create permission to minimize confusion and restore the property from before Kubectl 1.31 that using kubectl to exec / attach / portForward requires create permission

addressed by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134577 in 1.35.0+

comments.author: liggitt
comments.body:
Websocket exec via `get` permissions only have always been possible in Kubernetes (xref https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/78741)

kubectl specifically switching from spdy (using POST method / create verb) to websockets (using GET method / get verb) and therefore requiring a new permission (`get` verb) and no longer always requiring the `create` permission was not recognized as a side-effect, because the built-in roles that allow `pods/exec`, `pods/attach`, etc, grant _both_ `get` and `create` permissions. That happened in Kubectl 1.31+, and works against 1.30+ servers (which support the websocket subprotocol version kubectl attempts to use).

cc @kubernetes/sig-auth-leads for thoughts on whether there's anything we can do to make the required permissions more obvious and consistent regardless of whether spdy or websockets are used.

comments.author: luxas
comments.body: If it was easily possible technically, would using a `connect` verb be considered (or was, at the time)? After all, regardless of the request was get, post, or something else in the beginning, it hits the same connect function in the backend. That would UX-wise also avoid the problem of some RBAC rule of form `verb=get`, `resource=*`, `apiGroup=*` match e.g. `pods/exec`, most likely to the surprise of the policy author that thought they gave read-only privileges only.

comments.author: liggitt
comments.body:
> If it was easily possible technically, would using a connect verb be considered (or was, at the time)?

The authz layer doesn't know an HTTP `GET` to `pods/exec` is a connect, and an HTTP `GET` to `pods/log` is just a get.

`create` is more clearly a modifying verb, so I think the minimum distance from the current state back to a clearer state is to add a secondary authz check inside `pods/exec`, `pods/attach`, `pods/portforward` handlers to specifically enforce that.

I think that would be ~fine to do with an escape hatch for a few releases, and if it's going to be done, now is the time before too many releases of a websocket get-permission-only kubectl propagates too far.

> avoid the problem of some RBAC rule of form verb=get, resource=*, apiGroup=*

someone who granted wildcard permissions to all groups/resources like that also gave full read access to secrets and node proxy access to the kubelet API for any GET request 😱 

wildcard permissions are really not good, constraining to a get verb is no guarantee the granted user is super-limited in what they can do

title: DRA Extended Resource: support nodes where device plugin was uninstalled
need_summary: Whether the device-plugin-to-DRA transition bug can block correct scheduling and what fix path is being discussed, anchored on the Kubernetes device plugin KEP and PR #133727.
security_topic: kubelet device-plugin resource cleanup after uninstall
question_text:
### What happened?

[deployDevicePlugin](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/790393ae92e97262827d4f1fba24e8ae65bbada0/test/e2e/dra/deploy_device_plugin.go#L34) leaks the extended resource example.com/resource in node's status.Allocatable/Capacity. This causes conflicts for multiple tests using the extended resource in the same cluster.

### What did you expect to happen?

deployDevicePlugin does not leak the example.com/resource in node's status.Allocatable/Capacity, after the test deploying the device plugin completes, the example.com/resource should be cleaned up from node's status.Allocatalbe/Capacity.
answer_text:
No, it was not a design decision. [Device Plugin KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/3573-device-plugin) explicitly states that 
```
In general we expect Kubelet to remove any devices that are owned by
the failed device plugin from the node capacity.
We also expect node allocatable to be equal to node capacity.
```
which is good for us as we can consider current Kubelet behaviour as a bug and fix it.

security_topic: mitigation for node self-deletion via OwnerReferences manipulation
question_text: ### How do I mitigate this vulnerability?
answer_text:
This issue can be mitigated by upgrading to a kube-apiserver binary running one of patched minor versions for 1.31 through 1.33 listed below. These fixed versions have added functionality to the NodeRestriction admission controller to prevent node users from modifying their own OwnerReferences.

Alternatively, this vulnerability can be mitigated by enabling the OwnerReferencesPermissionEnforcement admission controller, which will prevent any user without delete permissions on an object from modifying the OwnerReferences on that object. thread_text:
ISSUE #133471: CVE-2025-5187: Nodes can delete themselves by adding an OwnerReference
Author: natherz97
Date: 2025-08-11T16:29:36Z
Labels: kind/bug, area/security, committee/security-response, needs-triage, official-cve-feed
State: closed

[c0]
CVSS Rating: [CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:L](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3-1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:L) - Medium (6.7)

A vulnerability exists in the NodeRestriction admission controller where node users can delete their corresponding node object by patching themselves with an OwnerReference to a cluster-scoped resource. If the OwnerReference resource does not exist or is subsequently deleted, the given node object will be deleted via garbage collection. By default, node users are authorized for create and patch requests but not delete requests against their node object. Since the NodeRestriction admission controller does not prevent patching OwnerReferences, a compromised node could leverage this vulnerability to delete and then recreate its node object. This would permit the node object to be recreated with modified taints or labels which are normally rejected by this plugin. Modifying taints or labels on a node could allow an attacker to control which pods are running on the compromised node.

### Am I vulnerable?

All clusters that have enabled the NodeRestriction but not the OwnerReferencesPermissionEnforcement admission controller are vulnerable. The OwnerReferencesPermissionEnforcement controller protects access to the OwnerReferences of an object so that only users with delete permission to the object can change it.

#### Affected Versions
kube-apiserver: <= v1.31.11
kube-apiserver: <= v1.32.7
kube-apiserver: <= v1.33.3
### How do I mitigate this vulnerability?

This issue can be mitigated by upgrading to a kube-apiserver binary running one of patched minor versions for 1.31 through 1.33 listed below. These fixed versions have added functionality to the NodeRestriction admission controller to prevent node users from modifying their own OwnerReferences. 

Alternatively, this vulnerability can be mitigated by enabling the OwnerReferencesPermissionEnforcement admission controller, which will prevent any user without delete permissions on an object from modifying the OwnerReferences on that object. Note that this admission controller will apply to all users and object types.

#### Fixed Versions
kube-apiserver: >= v1.31.12
kube-apiserver: >= v1.32.8
kube-apiserver: >= v1.33.4

### Detection

This issue can be detected on clusters which have NodeRestriction but not OwnerReferencesPermissionEnforcement enabled by analyzing API audit logs for node patch requests issued by node users which modify OwnerReferences. In normal operation, a Kubelet will never issue a patch request which modifies its own OwnerReferences.

If you find evidence that this vulnerability has been exploited, please contact [security@kubernetes.io](mailto:security@kubernetes.io)

#### Acknowledgements

This vulnerability was reported by Paul Viossat.

The issue was fixed and coordinated by: 

Sergey Kanzhelev @SergeyKanzhelev
Jordan Liggitt @liggitt
Marko Mudrinić @xmudrii

ISSUE #133441: Temporary volumes (emptyDir, configMap, secrets) created with 0777 permissions – Security concern and compliance question
Author: SaraLaguna333
Date: 2025-08-08T09:28:30Z
Labels: kind/bug, lifecycle/rotten, sig/security, needs-triage
State: closed

[c0]
### What happened?

Hello Kubernetes team,
A vulnerability scan (SHC) has flagged a potential misconfiguration (ID: RIES-693, also known as "Riesgo 55 en Misuri") due to temporary directories being created with 0777 permissions inside Kubernetes pods.

We have observed that:

    The issue affects volumes created from emptyDir, configMap, and secret.

    It is reproducible and not random, and seems to be part of Kubernetes' standard behavior.

    These directories are being created with world-writable (0777) permissions, which conflicts with various internal security and hardening policies.

    This behavior is not caused by the container runtime. We use CRI-O (Kubernetes v1.32.7), which is the recommended runtime, and the issue appears to originate in Kubernetes core.

We have reviewed the following related issue:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/125876

In that thread, it is acknowledged that Kubernetes is assigning these permissions, and there's a TODO in the codebase suggesting it is known but not yet addressed. However, it's still unclear whether:

    This behavior is intentional and accepted, or

    It is a pending security enhancement or known issue under consideration.
Request:
Due to compliance requirements, we kindly request one of the following:

    Confirmation that this behavior is expected and accepted by the Kubernetes project, ideally with links to relevant documentation or design decisions.

    OR, confirmation that this is a known issue, and any information about plans to address it or a suggested mitigation.

We need this as evidence that the issue has been escalated to the Kubernetes maintainers.
🔧 Environment:

    Kubernetes version: v1.32.7

    Container runtime: CRI-O

  Thank you

Thank you in advance for your time and guidance. We understand this may be a deeply technical or legacy-driven decision, but any clarification or support you can provide will be extremely helpful to us and likely to others in regulated industries.

Kind regards,

### What did you expect to happen?

We expected the temporary directories created by Kubernetes for emptyDir, configMap, and secret volumes to have more restrictive default permissions — for example, 0755 or 0700 — instead of 0777, which grants world-writable access.

This expectation is based on common security hardening practices and compliance standards, which typically discourage the use of world-writable permissions (0777) in production environments, especially for sensitive volumes managed by the container orchestration platform.

title: Segfault on e2e tests after 1.34 RC
need_summary: Whether the apiserver segfault was caused by deprecated metric handling on the 1.34 RC and what code change fixed it, anchored by pull request #133412 and the referenced metric deprecation docs/source.
security_topic: pre-release metric deprecation causing apiserver crash
question_text:
any idea why the panic was not caught in presubmit CI?

EDIT: or the related question, why did it start happening after the RC from yesterday and earlier?
answer_text:
The immediate issue is fixed by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133412, so this particular issue can be marked as fixed

There are three follow-ups I see:
1. Make the deprecation handling kick in on pre-release versions (probably >=1.x.0-beta.0) - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/133405#issuecomment-3164071474
2. Make the label removal more robust in general so all call sites are protected (wrapping DeleteLabelValues, etc) - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133410
3. Sweep for packages logicalhan has individual approval on and switch to the instrumentation leads alias where it makes sense - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133412#issuecomment-3163147582

Author: michaelasp

[c0]
### Which jobs are failing?

All kind tests are failing due to a segfault in the apiserver with the 1.34 rc

### Which tests are failing?

Many e2e tests running on the newest RC

### Since when has it been failing?

Since the release was cut and we bump the tag to 1.34

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-release-master-blocking#kind-master

Not fully sure but it seems due to these two commits conflicting with each other.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/131902/files

and 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/132965/files

One uses a metric that is deprecated in 1.34 and is causing a nil pointer exception, seems like that causes that metric to be set to nil but seems likely to be the case from the logs.

An easy fix might be to use the new metric defined by @serathius in the second PR. 

CC @liuxu623 who made the first change.

Seems likely to be a release blocker.

> [#133406](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133406) may be enough to fix the issue, just removing reference to the deprecated metric but want to make sure that is the correct path.

We would want to keep the data/behavior for both old and new metrics consistent (until we fully remove/delete the deprecated STABLE metric, which I am not sure whether we finalized on a process for, yet). Doing it for the new one but not the old one meanwhile is probably undesirable
---
[c6] @richabanker 2025-08-07T02:43:38Z:
The issue is that we call prom-client's `DeleteLabelValues()` [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/metrics/metrics.go#L227) for the deprecataed metric `apiserver_storage_objects` which panics because its not created/registered for versions > its deprecation_version(1.34.0)

To handle unregistered metrics, we might need something like https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133410 

If we want a quick fix we can just update the HELP text for `apiserver_storage_objects` in 1.34 to show our intention for deprecating it in future, at which point we

- should have a proper way to handle `DeleteLabelValues()` for unregistered metrics
- record the DeprecatedVersion to whatever the current version is then 
- remove all usages of the metric 3 releases after DeprecatedVersion

cc @serathius  @dgrisonnet  
---
[c7] @richabanker 2025-08-07T04:27:38Z:
Another option for a hot-fix: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133412 but this doesnt help us prevent this from happening again in future.
---
[c8] @serathius 2025-08-07T08:37:48Z:
> The issue is that we call prom-client's DeleteLabelValues() [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/metrics/metrics.go#L227) for the deprecated metric apiserver_storage_objects which panics because its not created/registered for versions > its deprecation_version(1.34.0)

Richa is right, the issue is broken `DeleteLabelValues` function that is not handling unregistered metrics in K8s metrics framework. K8s metrics definitions are wrappers for Prometheus client library. K8s adds metric lifecycle management that can prevent registration of metric. It's implemented with Prometheus definition is a substruct, for most calls we override functions and add handling for metric not being registered, however we forgot to do that for `DeleteLabelValues`. 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133412, that replaces broken `DeleteLabelValues` function with `Delete` that is overwritten to handle unregistered metrics, seems like the great short term fix. Thanks @richabanker 
---

> any idea why the panic was not caught in presubmit CI?

Metric was marked as deprecated for `1.34`. Maybe we don't run resubmits when we bumped K8s version to 1.34.0-rc0?
---
[c11] @neolit123 2025-08-07T12:25:53Z:
> > any idea why the panic was not caught in presubmit CI?
> 
> Metric was marked as deprecated for `1.34`. 

yes, but why didn't it start happening for 1.34 alpha or beta?

> Maybe we don't run resubmits when we bumped K8s version to 1.34.0-rc0?

the release bot just pushes a commit to mark the release, so there are no presubmits to catch such an issue:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/13ced7b7ddc2e4b86bcb098e7876030ae2eb8802
---
[c12] @serathius 2025-08-07T12:40:58Z:
> yes, but why didn't it start happening for 1.34 alpha or beta?

Guessing `1.34.0-alpha.0` < `1.34.0-beta.0` <  `1.34.0-rc.0` <= `1.34.0`? 

EDIT; didn't find evidence of that. Looks like all prereleases are treated the same https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/13ced7b7ddc2e4b86bcb098e7876030ae2eb8802/vendor/github.com/blang/semver/v4/semver.go#L145-L173
---
[c13] @neolit123 2025-08-07T12:48:03Z:
> > yes, but why didn't it start happening for 1.34 alpha or beta?
> 
> Guessing `1.34.0-alpha.0` < `1.34.0-beta.0` < `1.34.0-rc.0` <= `1.34.0`?

if there is a metric that is marked as deprecated for 1.34.0 in the logic that performs the version check it should consider all prereleases of the target release that would trigger the change of behavior. sounds like that area of the code is buggy if it triggered only after the RC and not for the alpha and beta earlier.

the consequence here of course is that k8s released a completely broken RC version apiserver.

---
[c14] @serathius 2025-08-07T12:54:07Z:
> if there is a metric that is marked as deprecated for 1.34.0 in the logic that performs the version check it should consider all prereleases of the target release that would trigger the change of behavior. sounds like that area of the code is buggy if it triggered only after the RC and not for the alpha and beta earlier.

Agree

[c15] @neolit123 2025-08-07T13:20:42Z:
where is the actual code that does the version checking for metric deprecation?
i found this, but not sure if that's it. this particular code seems problematic as it returns false for pre-releases.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/13ced7b7ddc2e4b86bcb098e7876030ae2eb8802/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/metrics/registry.go#L76

There are three follow-ups I see:
1. Make the deprecation handling kick in on pre-release versions (probably >=1.x.0-beta.0) - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/133405#issuecomment-3164071474
2. Make the label removal more robust in general so all call sites are protected (wrapping DeleteLabelValues, etc) - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133410
3. Sweep for packages logicalhan has individual approval on and switch to the instrumentation leads alias where it makes sense - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133412#issuecomment-3163147582

> 1. Make the deprecation handling kick in on pre-release versions (probably >=1.x.0-beta.0) - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/133405#issuecomment-3164071474

Separately, that utility needs to consider semver correctly.

> > 1. Make the deprecation handling kick in on pre-release versions (probably >=1.x.0-beta.0) - [Segfault on e2e tests after 1.34 RC #133405 (comment)](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/133405#issuecomment-3164071474)

comments.author: richabanker
comments.body:
The issue is that we call prom-client's `DeleteLabelValues()` [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/metrics/metrics.go#L227) for the deprecataed metric `apiserver_storage_objects` which panics because its not created/registered for versions > its deprecation_version(1.34.0)

To handle unregistered metrics, we might need something like https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133410 

If we want a quick fix we can just update the HELP text for `apiserver_storage_objects` in 1.34 to show our intention for deprecating it in future, at which point we

- should have a proper way to handle `DeleteLabelValues()` for unregistered metrics
- record the DeprecatedVersion to whatever the current version is then 
- remove all usages of the metric 3 releases after DeprecatedVersion

cc @serathius  @dgrisonnet

comments.author: richabanker
comments.body: Another option for a hot-fix: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133412 but this doesnt help us prevent this from happening again in future.

comments.author: serathius
comments.body:
> The issue is that we call prom-client's DeleteLabelValues() [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/metrics/metrics.go#L227) for the deprecated metric apiserver_storage_objects which panics because its not created/registered for versions > its deprecation_version(1.34.0)

Richa is right, the issue is broken `DeleteLabelValues` function that is not handling unregistered metrics in K8s metrics framework. K8s metrics definitions are wrappers for Prometheus client library. K8s adds metric lifecycle management that can prevent registration of metric. It's implemented with Prometheus definition is a substruct, for most calls we override functions and add handling for metric not being registered, however we forgot to do that for `DeleteLabelValues`. 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133412, that replaces broken `DeleteLabelValues` function with `Delete` that is overwritten to handle unregistered metrics, seems like the great short term fix. Thanks @richabanker

The immediate issue is fixed by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133412, so this particular issue can be marked as fixed

There are three follow-ups I see:
1. Make the deprecation handling kick in on pre-release versions (probably >=1.x.0-beta.0) - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/133405#issuecomment-3164071474
2. Make the label removal more robust in general so all call sites are protected (wrapping DeleteLabelValues, etc) - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133410
3. Sweep for packages logicalhan has individual approval on and switch to the instrumentation leads alias where it makes sense - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133412#issuecomment-3163147582

/close

I think "deprecatedVersion" is the wrong way to manage this, we need "hidden version", or else "deprecatedVersion" logic also needs to consider the stability level when computing which version to stop serving it at.

comments.author: AadiDev005
comments.body:
Hi @gdzzdesti,

Interesting find with the pprof analysis showing the memory increase tied to pod watching. From the flamegraphs @haosdent shared, the difference seems more subtle than your initial prometheus metrics suggested (27.36M vs 30.98M), but the pattern is definitely worth investigating.

A few thoughts on this:

1. The scheduler maintains watch connections and internal state for all pods - after uninstalling, some cached data structures might not be getting properly cleaned up
2. With 100 replicas per StatefulSet, that's quite a bit of pod metadata to track

Have you tried reproducing this with smaller pod counts to see if it scales linearly? Also curious if forcing a GC (`runtime.GC()`) or waiting longer shows any memory recovery.

This could be a legitimate watch cache cleanup issue in the scheduler's informer system.

comments.author: ravisastryk
comments.body:
I discovered now that memory leak is potentially happening in the Kubernetes framework, in particular pods removal code path. 

It was caused by improper slice element removal in the [removeFromSlice()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/13ced7b7ddc2e4b86bcb098e7876030ae2eb8802/pkg/scheduler/framework/types.go#L363)
When pods were removed from NodeInfo slices (Pods, PodsWithAffinity, PodsWithRequiredAntiAffinity), the function was:

1. Moving the last element to the deleted position `s[i] = s[len(s)-1]`
2. Shrinking slice `s = s[:len(s) - 1]`
3. But not clearing the moved element reference. This is the fix I am proposing to explicitly clear the reference via `s[len(s)-1] = nil`

Can someone validate my hypothesis in this https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133411
cc @AadiDev005 @macsko

comments.author: AadiDev005
comments.body:
[@ravisastryk](https://github.com/ravisastryk)! This makes total sense now.

I was thinking it had to be something with the watch cache not cleaning up properly  it's that removeFromSlice() function. The fact that it's not clearing the reference after moving elements is such a classic Go gotcha.

This explains exactly what we're seeing - memory stays high after pod deletion because those PodInfo objects are still referenced even though they're "removed" from the slice. With 100 replicas and anti-affinity rules, that's a lot of objects stuck in memory.

The fix looks right - just need that s[len(s)-1] = nil to let the GC do its job. Have you had a chance to test this against the original reproduction case yet? Would be great to see the before/after memory profiles.

comments.author: ravisastryk
comments.body:
Thank you @AadiDev005  and @olderTaoist. yes, I have seen similar Go-related gotchas in production especially when it comes to dealing with slices and I can see how this fix helps mitigate the memory leak. My plan is to add unit tests, specifically targeting the memory leak so that I can demonstrate how the fix improves things, and also include some benchmark results after fixing tests.

I would appreciate validation from @olderTaoist and the original reporter in a production setting. That said, from a regression standpoint, it would be best to include unit tests. I will take it up on that front.

Author: Brett A C Sheffield (Librecast) <bacs@librecast.net>

title: CVE-2025-7342: VM images built with Kubernetes Image Builder Nutanix or OVA providers use default credentials for Windows images if user did not override
need_summary: Whether Kubernetes Image Builder v0.1.44 and earlier expose a default-credentials window in Windows images built with the Nutanix or OVA providers, and the answer rests on CVE-2025-7342 plus the fixed-version reference to v0.1.45 and PR #1800.
security_topic: applicability of a vulnerability to specific image-builder providers and versions
question_text: Am I vulnerable?
answer_text:
Clusters using virtual machine Windows images built with Kubernetes Image Builder (https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/image-builder) version v0.1.44 or earlier are affected if built with the Nutanix or OVA provider.

VMs using images built with all other providers are not affected by this issue.
thread_text:
ISSUE #133115: CVE-2025-7342: VM images built with Kubernetes Image Builder Nutanix or OVA providers use default credentials for Windows images if user did not override
Author: ritazh
Date: 2025-07-21T23:22:19Z
Labels: kind/bug, area/security, sig/cluster-lifecycle, committee/security-response, triage/accepted, official-cve-feed
State: closed

[c0]
CVSS Rating High 7.5: [CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H)

A security issue was discovered in the Kubernetes Image Builder where default credentials are enabled during the Windows image build process when using the Nutanix or VMware OVA providers. These credentials, which allow root access, are disabled at the conclusion of the build. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if their nodes use VM images created via the Image Builder project and the vulnerability was exploited during the build process, which requires an attacker to access the build VM and modify the image while the build is in progress.

### Am I vulnerable?

Clusters using virtual machine Windows images built with Kubernetes Image Builder (https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/image-builder) version v0.1.44 or earlier are affected if built with the Nutanix or OVA provider.

VMs using images built with all other providers are not affected by this issue.

To determine the version of Image Builder you are using, use one of the following methods:
- For git clones of the image builder repository:
```
    cd <local path to image builder repo>
    make version
```
- For installations using a tarball download:
```
    cd <local path to install location>
    grep -o v0\\.[0-9.]* RELEASE.md | head -1
```
- For a container image release:
    `docker run --rm <image pull spec> version`
  or
    `podman run --rm <image pull spec> version`
  or look at the image tag specified, in the case of an official image such as `registry.k8s.io/scl-image-builder/cluster-node-image-builder-amd64:v0.1.44`


#### Affected Versions

- Kubernetes Image Builder versions <= v0.1.44

### How do I mitigate this vulnerability?
Rebuild any affected images using a fixed version of Image Builder. Fixed in Kubernetes Image Builder release v0.1.45
Re-deploy the fixed images to any affected VMs or use image-builder v0.1.41 (February 2025) or later, and set the `admin_password` JSON variable.
Prior to upgrading, this vulnerability can be mitigated by changing the password of the Administrator account on affected VMs:
`net user Administrator <new-password>`

#### Fixed Versions

Fixed in Kubernetes Image Builder release v0.1.45 https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/image-builder/pull/1800


### Detection

`Get-LocalUser -Name Administrator | Select-Object Name,Enabled,SID,Lastlogon | Format-List`

If you find evidence that this vulnerability has been exploited, please contact security@kubernetes.io

## Additional Details

The fixed version requires users to specify a password in the WINDOWS_ADMIN_PASSWORD environment variable or in the `admin_password` JSON variable. If both are empty, then the image builder would not build the image and return an error.

#### Acknowledgements

This vulnerability was reported by Abdel Adim Oisfi, Davide Silvetti, Nicolò Daprelà, Paolo Cavaglià, Pietro Tirenna from Shielder.

The issue was fixed and coordinated by Matt Boersma of the Image Builder project.
